<!-- docs/install-packages.md -->

# Install packages and the Claude skill

> The Windows and Linux install packages, the Docker image, and the skill file that teaches an AI assistant in another project how to use KarelaDB.

- Category: Getting started
- Keywords: install, installer, package, zip, tar.gz, install.sh, install.ps1, PATH, systemd, service, Docker, image, container, docker stop, docker rm, stop-timeout, restart unless-stopped, HEALTHCHECK, healthy, connection refused, retry, 503, Retry-After, KARELADB\_DRAIN\_TIMEOUT, last shutdown, not clean, uninstall, Claude, AI, skill, kareladb skill, kareladb skill install, --dir, --url, --home, KARELADB\_URL, token file, 0600, /skill.md, agent, assistant, KARELADB\_TOKEN, KARELADB\_MEMORY, KARELADB\_MEMORY\_LIMIT, KARELADB\_READER\_YIELD, KARELADB\_SNAPSHOT\_READS, KARELADB\_CORE\_DUMPS, KARELADB\_CORE\_KEEP, core dump, crash, gdb, kdb.debug, KARELADB\_DATA\_DIR, KARELADB\_CONFIG, KARELADB\_BACKUP\_SCHEDULE, KARELADB\_BACKUP\_COMMAND, GLIBC\_TUNABLES, kareladb.conf, volume
- See also: [Quick start](quick-start.md), [kareladb serve](cli-serve.md), [Web console](web-console.md), [HTTP API overview](http-overview.md), [Keeping kareladb serve safe](server-security.md)

KarelaDB ships as one program and three folders of plain files next to it: the web console, the help pages and the Claude skill. There is nothing else to install - no runtime, no libraries, no service to configure first. There are three ways to get it onto a machine.

| Way | You get | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| The Windows package | `kareladb-<version>-windows-x64.zip` | a desktop or a Windows server |
| The Linux package | `kareladb-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz`, built static so it runs on any distribution | a VPS or a Linux desktop |
| The Docker image | a small Alpine image with the program and its folders | a server you would rather not install anything on |

An unpacked package looks like this:

```text
kareladb-<version>-<os>-x64/
  kareladb.exe (Windows) or kareladb (Linux)   the program - nothing else is inside it
  web/                               the web console
  help/                              the help pages (missing when the package was made without them)
  skill/skill.md                     the Claude skill
  install.ps1 or install.sh, kareladb.conf.example, README.md
```

<a id="windows"></a>

## Windows

Unpack the zip and run the installer from the folder it made:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

It copies `kareladb.exe` and its `web`, `help` and `skill` folders into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\kareladb`, adds that folder to **your** PATH (no administrator rights needed) and writes the [Claude skill](install-packages.md#skill). Add `-Token my-secret` to save your token beside the skill, in a file only you can read.

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-Prefix <folder>` | where the program goes | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\kareladb` |
| `-Token <secret>` | the token, saved in the file `token` beside the skill | `$env:KARELADB_TOKEN` |
| `-Data <folder>` | the data folder it suggests | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\kdb\data` |
| `-NoPath` | do not touch PATH | - |
| `-NoSkill` | do not write the skill | - |

Uninstalling is deleting that folder and taking it off your PATH. Nothing is registered with Windows.

<a id="linux"></a>

## Linux

Unpack the tar.gz and run the installer from the folder it made:

```bash
./install.sh                                              # just you: ~/.local/bin, folders in ~/.local/share/kareladb
sudo ./install.sh --system                                # everyone: /usr/local/bin, folders in /usr/local/share/kareladb
sudo ./install.sh --system --service --token my-secret    # ...and start it at boot
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--system` | install into `/usr/local` instead of `~/.local` | - |
| `--prefix <folder>` | install somewhere else | `~/.local` |
| `--service` | write a systemd unit and start it (needs root and `--token`) | - |
| `--token <secret>` | the token for the service and the skill | `$KARELADB_TOKEN` |
| `--data <folder>` | the data folder | `/var/lib/kdb` or `~/.local/share/kareladb` |

With `--service` the server runs as its own `kareladb` user, is restarted if it stops, and can write to its data folder and nowhere else. The unit file holds the token, so it is readable only by root.

```bash
systemctl status kareladb
journalctl -u kareladb -f
```

<a id="folders"></a>

## Where kareladb finds the console, the help and the skill

The web console, the help pages and the Claude skill are files, so a new console or help needs the files copied, not a new program. `kareladb` looks for each folder in this order and uses the first one that has its files in it (`index.html`, or `skill.md`):

| Order | Web console | Help pages | Claude skill |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. `kareladb.conf` | `"web_dir"` | `"help_dir"` | `"skill_dir"` |
| 2. environment | `KARELADB_WEB_DIR` | `KARELADB_HELP_DIR` | `KARELADB_SKILL_DIR` |
| 3. next to the program | `web/` | `help/` | `skill/` |
| 4. `share/kareladb` beside the program folder | `../share/kareladb/web` | `../share/kareladb/help` | `../share/kareladb/skill` |
| 5. a source checkout (`build/bin/kareladb`) | `web/console` | `docs/help/site` | `.claude/skills/kareladb` |

- The console's **Settings** page shows the folders in use and what chose each one. They are read-only there.
- Files are read when they are asked for, so copying a new help build into `help/` shows at the next page load, without a restart.
- A folder that is missing does not stop the server. The HTTP API works, `http://127.0.0.1:9900/` says the console is not installed and lists the folders it looked in, and `/help/` says how to build the help.

A `kareladb.conf` that names all three:

```json
{
  "data_dir": "E:/kdb-data",
  "web_dir": "E:/kdb/web",
  "help_dir": "E:/kdb/help",
  "skill_dir": "E:/kdb/skill"
}
```

<a id="docker"></a>

## Docker

```bash
docker run -d --name kareladb -p 9900:9900 -p 8832:8832 \
  -e KARELADB_TOKEN=<token> -v kdb-data:/data kareladb
```

The data lives in the named volume `kdb-data`, so removing and recreating the container does not lose it. The server refuses to start without `KARELADB_TOKEN`: the image listens on all addresses, so a published port can reach it, and KarelaDB does not do that without a secret.

The image holds `/usr/local/bin/kareladb` and its folders in `/usr/local/share/kareladb/web`, `help` and `skill` (named by `KARELADB_WEB_DIR`, `KARELADB_HELP_DIR` and `KARELADB_SKILL_DIR`). The image build only compiles `kareladb` and copies those folders from the source tree, so run the help build first when the help pages should be in it.

- Add `--restart unless-stopped` so the server comes back by itself after Docker or the computer restarts.
- The image has a health check: `docker ps` shows `healthy` once the HTTP port answers `GET /health`. While the server is stopping, `/health` answers 503.
- Anything after the image name is added to `kareladb serve`, for example `... kareladb --threads 4`.

The settings of the image, all given with `-e NAME=value`:

| Variable | Meaning | Default in the image |
|---|---|---|
| `KARELADB_TOKEN` | the secret every request sends as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The start script passes it as `--token`; the program itself reads no `KARELADB_TOKEN`. | none: required |
| `KARELADB_MEMORY` | `--memory`, in MB (passed as the flag) | `256` |
| `KARELADB_MEMORY_LIMIT` | one limit for everything the server holds ([memory limit](cli-serve.md#memory-limit)), like `3GB` | 85% of the container's memory limit, else of Docker's memory |
| `KARELADB_DATA_DIR` | the data folder | `/data` |
| `KARELADB_CONFIG` | the settings file (passed as `--config`) | `/data/kareladb.conf` |
| `KARELADB_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` | how long running requests may finish on a stop | `5s` |
| `KARELADB_READER_YIELD` | `on`: reads do not wait for a long trigger or transaction ([--reader-yield](cli-serve.md#kareladb-serve)). `off`: they wait. | `on` |
| `KARELADB_SNAPSHOT_READS` | `on`: a read of a table being written reads a snapshot of the committed rows and does not wait ([--snapshot-reads](cli-serve.md#kareladb-serve)) | `off` |
| `KARELADB_PER_TABLE_READS` | `off`: every read waits for every writer, as before ([--per-table-reads](cli-serve.md#kareladb-serve)) | `on` |
| `KARELADB_READ_ONLY_CALLS` | `off`: every `CALL` is a transaction, also one that only reads ([--read-only-calls](cli-serve.md#kareladb-serve)) | `on` |
| `KARELADB_CORE_DUMPS` | `on`: a crash leaves a core dump in `/data/_logs/cores` (kareladb runs from that folder). At the next start the dump is renamed with its time. `off`: no dumps. The unstripped program for reading one is `/usr/local/lib/kdb/kdb.debug` (`gdb kdb.debug core.<time>`). | `on` |
| `KARELADB_CORE_KEEP` | how many old core dumps are kept; a dump is about as big as the server's memory | `2` |
| every other `KARELADB_*` variable of `kareladb serve` | as listed in [every option](cli-serve.md#all-options), for example `KARELADB_HTTP_THREADS`, `KARELADB_TIMER_WORKERS`, `KARELADB_CACHE_MB`, `KARELADB_TIMEZONE` | the program's defaults |
| `GLIBC_TUNABLES` | for example `glibc.malloc.arena_max=8`: how many memory arenas the C library keeps (fewer than the query threads makes concurrent queries wait for each other's allocations; 2 arenas halved the request rate of 8 clients) (see `allocator_arena_max` in [/api/stats](http-server-info.md#api-stats)). With `trim_threshold` set, KarelaDB puts glibc's mmap line at 32 MB, where glibc would move it itself (`allocator_mmap_threshold`) | KarelaDB chooses |

A fuller run line, as a long-running server uses it:

```bash
docker run -d --name kareladb --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 60 \
  -p 9900:9900 -p 8832:8832 \
  -e KARELADB_TOKEN=<token> -e KARELADB_MEMORY=1536 -e KARELADB_READER_YIELD=on \
  -e GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.arena_max=8:glibc.malloc.trim_threshold=67108864 \
  -v kdb-data:/data kareladb
```

On Windows, `-v "D:\kdb_data:/data"` puts the data in a Windows folder instead of a named volume.

<a id="docker-settings"></a>

### The data folder and kareladb.conf in the container

- The image passes the data folder as the environment variable `KARELADB_DATA_DIR`, **not** as `--data-dir`. A command-line flag always wins over what the console's [Settings page](console-settings.md) saves, so a flag would make that page read-only. With the variable, `/data` is the default and an admin can still choose another folder in the console.
- `kareladb.conf` is `/data/kareladb.conf`, inside the volume. A setting saved on the Settings page survives `docker rm` and a new image.
- A data folder chosen on the Settings page must be under a mounted volume too. Anywhere else is in the container's own layer and is thrown away with the container.
- Backups go to `/data/_backups`, inside the volume, with no setting. Turn on a schedule with `-e KARELADB_BACKUP_SCHEDULE="daily 02:00"` (or the Settings page), and copy each backup off the machine with `-e KARELADB_BACKUP_COMMAND="..."` - the tool it runs (rclone, aws) must be in the image ([backup schedule](backup-schedule.md#backup-command)).

<a id="docker-stop"></a>

### Stopping and restarting the container

| Command | What KarelaDB gets | Next start says |
|---|---|---|
| `docker stop kareladb`, container run **with** `--stop-timeout 60` | SIGTERM, then a kill after 60 s | `last shutdown: clean` |
| `docker stop -t 60 kareladb` | SIGTERM, then a kill after 60 s | `last shutdown: clean` |
| `docker stop kareladb`, container run **without** `--stop-timeout` | SIGTERM, then a kill after Docker's default wait - seen as short as **1 s** | `clean` only if nothing was running |
| `docker rm -f kareladb`, `docker kill kareladb` | a kill at once | `last shutdown: not clean (crash or kill)` |

An image cannot choose how long Docker waits, so give the container `--stop-timeout` when you create it. Without it, a stop while a request runs, or while a big database closes, ends in a kill.

On SIGTERM the server:

1. keeps the port open and lets requests that are already running finish, up to `KARELADB_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (5 s in the image);
2. answers every new request with **503** and `Retry-After: 2`;
3. cancels what still runs (a writer that waits for a busy table stops waiting too), closes every database side by side and writes the clean-shutdown mark.

A kill is safe too - every confirmed write is in the log - but the next start has to replay the log. So stop the container before you remove it:

```bash
docker stop -t 60 kareladb && docker rm kareladb
docker run -d --name kareladb --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 60 \
  -e KARELADB_DRAIN_TIMEOUT=30s -e KARELADB_TOKEN=<token> \
  -p 9900:9900 -p 8832:8832 -v kdb-data:/data kareladb
```

- `--stop-timeout 60` makes a plain `docker stop` (and Docker's own restart) wait 60 s. Keep `KARELADB_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` well below it, so closing the databases still fits.
- The server log shows `databases closed cleanly (N ms)`. If N gets close to the stop timeout, give it more.
- With Docker Compose the same is `stop_grace_period: 60s` on the service.

<a id="docker-clients"></a>

### What a client should do

While the container is stopped and started again there is a short gap, about 2 s on a laptop.

| The client sees | Meaning | Do |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP **503** with `Retry-After` | the server is stopping; the request was not run | wait that many seconds, send it again |
| **connection refused** | the server is not listening yet (or any more) | wait a second, try again |
| the connection closed before a reply | the request was cut off | send it again |

- A write that was cut off, or answered 503, is rolled back as a whole: no row of it is saved. Sending the same `/write`, `/imp` or `/exec` again is safe.
- A request that was already running when the stop began gets its real answer, then the connection closes. Open a new one for the next request.
- Retry refused connections, not only HTTP errors. A loader that gives up on the first refused connection stops at every restart.

<a id="skill"></a>

## The Claude skill

Claude Code, or any other AI assistant, working in **some other project** has no idea KarelaDB exists. It will not guess the port, the token, the shape of `/exec` or where the help is. A *skill file* tells it, once, and every project on the machine benefits.

The installers write it for you. To do it by hand, or again after the address or token changed:

Syntax:

```sql
kareladb skill
kareladb skill install [--dir <folder>] [--url <address>] [--token <secret>] [--home <checkout>]
```

```bash
kareladb skill install                                  # writes ~/.claude/skills/kareladb/SKILL.md
kareladb skill install --token <token> --home /srv/kdb-source
kareladb skill                                          # print it instead, to pipe somewhere
```

**Installed the skill before the KarelaDB name?** After `kareladb skill install`, delete the old folder `~/.claude/skills/kdb` (with its `token` file). Otherwise the assistant has two skills for the same thing, and the old one is never updated.

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--dir <folder>` | where to write `SKILL.md` | `~/.claude/skills/kareladb` |
| `--url <address>` | the address the assistant should use | `$KARELADB_URL`, else `http://localhost:9900` |
| `--token <secret>` | the token, saved in the file `token` beside `SKILL.md` (see below) | `$KARELADB_TOKEN` |
| `--home <folder>` | a source checkout, so the assistant can read `docs/help/topics/` | - |

**Command line: Install into a folder of your choice, with another address**

```bash
kareladb skill install --dir my-skills/kareladb --url http://kdb.example.lan:9900
```

Output:

```text
wrote my-skills/kareladb/SKILL.md
Claude Code picks it up in any project the next time it starts.
```

**The token is never written into `SKILL.md`.** An assistant may quote that file, or you may copy it somewhere, so it only says where the token is. The token goes into its own file, `token`, in the same folder:

| | `SKILL.md` | `token` |
|---|---|---|
| holds | the skill, the address, the paths, **where** the token file is | the token, on one line |
| who can read it | like any of your files | only you: mode `0600` on Linux and macOS, an owner-only ACL on Windows |

Run without a token, `kareladb skill install` leaves an existing `token` file alone and still points to it. A `SKILL.md` written by an older build (then still called `kdb`) held the token in clear: run `kareladb skill install` again to replace it.

`--dir` is **refused** when it is, or is inside, a folder the server hands out without a login: the skill folder (`GET /skill.md`), the console folder or the help folder, wherever `kareladb` looks for them ([the folders](install-packages.md#folders)). A token there could be fetched by anyone who reaches the server.

The text is the file `skill/skill.md` next to the program, found the same way as the [other folders](install-packages.md#folders), so this works with no source folder and no network.

A running server also hands the same text out, without a token, at `GET /skill.md`. That is how a machine that can only reach the server over the network gets it:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/kareladb
curl -s http://your-server:9900/skill.md -o ~/.claude/skills/kareladb/SKILL.md
```

From Docker, ask the program inside the container:

```bash
docker exec kareladb kareladb skill > ~/.claude/skills/kareladb/SKILL.md
```

Claude Code reads the folder when it starts, so open a new terminal afterwards.

<a id="building"></a>

## Building the packages yourself

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --target kareladb
node tools/help/build_help.mjs --kdb build/bin/kareladb.exe   # the help pages -> docs/help/site (runs every example)
cpack --config build/CPackConfig.cmake          # -> dist/kareladb-<version>-<os>-<arch>
```

The Linux package is built inside the Docker image, which also links it static:

```bash
docker build --target package -o dist -f docker/Dockerfile .
```

A package holds the program, its `web`, `help` and `skill` folders, the installer and `kareladb.conf.example`. No source, no tests, no build folder. The help build is its own step: without it the package has no `help` folder, and `/help` says how to add one.

# Quick start

> Get kareladb, make a database, create a table, add rows, query them and open the web console.

- Category: Getting started
- Keywords: install, build, first steps, getting started, hello world, kareladb version, kareladb sql, kareladb shell, kareladb serve, console, sample data, tutorial
- See also: [Install packages and the Claude skill](install-packages.md), [SQL basics](sql-basics.md), [Sample data](sample-data.md), [Databases and the data folder](databases.md), [CREATE TABLE](create-table.md), [INSERT](insert.md), [Web console](web-console.md), [kareladb serve](cli-serve.md), [What's new](whats-new.md)

KarelaDB is one program: `kareladb` (`kareladb.exe` on Windows), with three folders of plain files next to it: `web/` (the web console), `help/` (these pages) and `skill/` (the Claude skill). It keeps each **database** in a folder. You talk to it with **SQL** (the language of databases). This page takes about 10 minutes.

KarelaDB is a general-purpose database: market and time-series data, sensor readings, logs and metrics, accounting, users and logins, app backends. A small example: a table of daily stock prices, three rows, and a query.

**Example: Your first table, rows and query**

```sql
CREATE TABLE ochl_day (
  time TIMESTAMP, symbol SYMBOL,
  open DOUBLE, high DOUBLE, low DOUBLE, close DOUBLE, volume DOUBLE
) TIMESERIES(time) PARTITION BY YEAR DEDUP KEY (symbol, time);

INSERT INTO ochl_day VALUES
  ('2026-09-09', 'CITY', 512, 512.4, 504, 504.6, 182390),
  ('2026-09-10', 'CITY', 504.6, 507, 500.7, 504.9, 183040),
  ('2026-09-10', 'COAST', 380.5, 382, 375.2, 376.1, 186200);

SELECT time, symbol, close FROM ochl_day WHERE symbol = 'CITY';
```

Result:


|---|---|---|

| 2026-09-10T00:00:00.000Z | CITY | 504.9 |

(2 rows)

<a id="get-kdb"></a>

## Get KarelaDB

There are three ways. Pick one.

| Way | You run | Then |
|---|---|---|
| An install package | unpack `kareladb-<version>-windows-x64.zip` (or the Linux `.tar.gz`) and run `install.ps1` (or `install.sh`) | `kareladb` is on your PATH, with its `web`, `help` and `skill` folders |
| Docker | `docker run` with the image `kareladb` (below) | the server runs on port 9900, the PostgreSQL port on 8832 |
| Build from the source | `cmake` (below) | the program is in `build\bin\kareladb.exe` |

[Install packages](install-packages.md) explains the packages and the Docker image in full.

<a id="docker"></a>

### Docker

Syntax:

```sql
docker run -d --name kareladb -p 9900:9900 -p 8832:8832 -e KARELADB_TOKEN=<secret> -v <data>:/data kareladb
```

The image holds the program and its three folders. Make it once from the source folder with `docker build -t kareladb -f docker/Dockerfile .`. The data stays in the volume, so a new container keeps it.

- **Notes:** the server does not start without `KARELADB_TOKEN`. Paste the token into the console's token box, or send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Add `--restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 60` so it comes back after a restart and stops cleanly. See [Docker](install-packages.md#docker).

```bash
docker run -d --name kareladb --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 60 \
  -p 9900:9900 -p 8832:8832 -e KARELADB_TOKEN=my-secret -v kdb-data:/data kareladb
curl http://127.0.0.1:9900/health
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:9900> and go on at [Open the web console](#console): the console and the HTTP API do everything the `kareladb sql` steps below do.

<a id="build"></a>

### Build from the source

Syntax:

```sql
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --target kareladb
```

Build the program from the KarelaDB source folder. You need CMake, Ninja and a C++17 compiler (on Windows: MSYS2 UCRT64). KarelaDB needs no other libraries.

- **Returns:** the program `build\bin\kareladb.exe` (Linux and macOS: `build/bin/kareladb`).
- **Notes:** a `kareladb` run from `build\bin` finds the console, the help and the skill in the source folder by itself (`web/console`, `docs/help/site`, `.claude/skills/kareladb`). To copy it to another PC, copy `kareladb.exe` together with the folders `web`, `help` and `skill`, or make a package. Without `web/` the HTTP API still works, but `http://127.0.0.1:9900/` says the console is not installed. See [where kareladb finds them](install-packages.md#folders). [Chapter 1](../tutorial/01-install.md) explains every step.

```powershell
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --target kareladb
$env:Path = "$PWD\build\bin;" + $env:Path
```

Check that it works:


<a id="first-database"></a>

## Your first database

Syntax:

```sql
kareladb sql database "SQL"
```

`kareladb sql` opens a database, runs the SQL, prints the result and closes the database. When the database does not exist yet, KarelaDB makes a new empty one.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `database` | name or folder | a database name like `shop`, or a folder path like `D:\kdb\shop` |
| `"SQL"` | text | one or more statements, separated by `;` |

- **Returns:** the result of each statement. Exit code `0` means OK, `1` means an error.
- **Notes:** a name without `\`, `/`, `:` or `.` means a database in the data folder, if one with that name is there; else a folder with that name in the current folder. See [databases](databases.md).

**Command line: Make a table in a new database, add a row, read it**

```bash
kareladb sql shop "CREATE TABLE brokers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name STRING NOT NULL)"
kareladb sql shop "INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (58, 'Northgate Securities'), (45, 'Imperial Securities')"
kareladb sql shop "SELECT id, name FROM brokers ORDER BY id"
```

Output:

`> kareladb sql shop "CREATE TABLE brokers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name STRING NOT NULL)"`

```text
table 'brokers' created
```

`> kareladb sql shop "INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (58, 'Northgate Securities'), (45, 'Imperial Securities')"`

```text
2 row(s) inserted
```

`> kareladb sql shop "SELECT id, name FROM brokers ORDER BY id"`

```text
id | name                
---+---------------------
45 | Imperial Securities 
58 | Northgate Securities
(2 rows, 0.2 ms)
```

A mistake gives a clear message and exit code 1:

**Command line: A typing mistake in a table name** (shows an error)

```bash
kareladb sql shop "CREATE TABLE brokers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name STRING NOT NULL)"
kareladb sql shop "SELECT * FROM brokerz"
```

Output:

`> kareladb sql shop "CREATE TABLE brokers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name STRING NOT NULL)"`

```text
table 'brokers' created
```

`> kareladb sql shop "SELECT * FROM brokerz"`

```text
error: line 1, column 15: table or view 'brokerz' does not exist
```

exit code 1

<a id="first-sql"></a>

## CREATE TABLE, INSERT and SELECT

Syntax:

```sql
CREATE TABLE name (column TYPE [rules], ...) [TIMESERIES(time_column) ...]
INSERT INTO name VALUES (value, ...), (value, ...)
SELECT columns FROM name [WHERE condition]
```

The three statements you use most. `CREATE TABLE` makes a table. `INSERT` adds rows. `SELECT` reads rows.

- There are two kinds of tables: **relational** (lists of things, like users) and **time-series** (rows with a time, like prices). See [CREATE TABLE](create-table.md).
- Text and times go in single quotes: `'CITY'`, `'2026-09-10'`.
- KarelaDB shows times in UTC (the `Z` at the end). Write a local time with its zone offset, for example `+05:45` (Nepal) or `-04:00` (New York).

**Example: App users: a relational table**

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id    LONG PRIMARY KEY AUTO,
  email STRING NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name  STRING
);
INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('ram@example.com', 'Ram'), ('sita@example.com', 'Sita');
SELECT id, email, name FROM users;
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE users (`

```text
table 'users' created
```

`INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('ram@example.com', 'Ram'), ('sita@example.com', 'Sita')`

```text
2 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT id, email, name FROM users`

| id (LONG) | email (STRING) | name (STRING) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ram@example.com | Ram |
| 2 | sita@example.com | Sita |

(2 rows)

**Example: A local time goes in with its offset (+05:45) and comes out in UTC**

```sql
CREATE TABLE live_prices (time TIMESTAMP, symbol SYMBOL, ltp DOUBLE) TIMESERIES(time);
INSERT INTO live_prices VALUES ('2026-09-10T11:00:00+05:45', 'CITY', 513.0);
SELECT time, symbol, ltp FROM live_prices;
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE live_prices (`

```text
table 'live_prices' created
```

`INSERT INTO live_prices VALUES ('2026-09-10T11:00:00+05:45', 'CITY', 513.0)`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT time, symbol, ltp FROM live_prices`

| time (TIMESTAMP) | symbol (SYMBOL) | ltp (DOUBLE) |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-10T05:15:00.000Z | CITY | 513 |

(1 row)

<a id="shell"></a>

## kareladb shell

Syntax:

```sql
kareladb shell [database]
```

A prompt where you type SQL. End each statement with `;`. A statement can use many lines. Commands that start with a dot (`.tables`, `.help`, `.exit`) need no `;`.

- **Notes:** without a database name, the shell opens the database `default` in the data folder. There you can also use `CREATE DATABASE` and `USE`.

**Command line: Type SQL in the shell**

```bash
kareladb shell shop
> CREATE TABLE posts (id LONG PRIMARY KEY AUTO, author STRING, body STRING);
> INSERT INTO posts (author, body) VALUES ('ram', 'CITY dividend looks good.');
> .tables
> SELECT id, author, body FROM posts;
> .exit
```

Output:

```text
KarelaDB 0.2.0-dev shell on shop
End statements with ';'. Type .help for commands, .exit to quit.
kareladb> table 'posts' created
kareladb> 1 row(s) inserted
kareladb> name  | kind       | partition | columns | rows
------+------------+-----------+---------+-----
posts | relational | NONE      |       3 |    1
(1 row, 0.0 ms)
kareladb> id | author | body                     
---+--------+--------------------------
 1 | ram    | CITY dividend looks good.
(1 row, 0.1 ms)
kareladb>
```

## Open the web console (kareladb serve)

Syntax:

```sql
kareladb serve [database] [--port 9900]
```

Starts the server. Open <http://127.0.0.1:9900> in a browser. Type SQL, press **Ctrl+Enter**, and see a grid or a chart. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop the server.

- **Notes:** while the server runs, other `kareladb` commands cannot open the same database. Use the console or the HTTP API then. Without a database name, the server serves every database in the data folder. The same server answers PostgreSQL tools on port 8832 and serves these help pages at <http://127.0.0.1:9900/help/>. See [kareladb serve](cli-serve.md) and [web console](web-console.md).
- **In Docker** the server is already running: open <http://127.0.0.1:9900> and paste your `KARELADB_TOKEN` into the token box.

<!-- docs/sql-basics.md -->

# SQL basics

> How KarelaDB reads SQL text: statements, names, text, numbers, TRUE/FALSE/NULL, comments, errors and reserved words.

- Category: Getting started
- Keywords: syntax, statement, semicolon, ;, case, upper case, lower case, identifier, name, quoted name, double quotes, string, text, single quote, escape quote, number, integer, float, scientific notation, boolean, constant, comment, --, /\*, error message, line and column, syntax error, reserved word, keyword, three-valued logic, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, unknown, alias
- See also: [Quick start](quick-start.md), [Operators](operators.md), [Conditional and NULL functions](functions-conditional.md), [Column types](column-types.md), [SELECT](select.md), [WHERE](where.md)

**SQL** is the language you use to talk to KarelaDB. A **statement** is one command, like `SELECT` or `INSERT`. This page shows the small rules that every statement follows.

**Example: Names, text, numbers, NULL and a comment in one query**

```sql
-- the price of one CITY share, and a note
SELECT 'CITY' AS symbol,
       512.45 AS "Last Price",   /* a name with a space needs double quotes */
       100 AS quantity,
       512.45 * 100 AS amount,
       'City''s bank' AS note,
       NULL AS broker;
```

Result:

| symbol (STRING) | Last Price (DOUBLE) | quantity (LONG) | amount (DOUBLE) | note (STRING) | broker (STRING) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CITY | 512.45 | 100 | 51245 | City's bank | NULL |

(1 row)

<a id="statements"></a>

## Statements and ;

Syntax:

```sql
statement ; statement ; ...
```

A text can hold many statements. Put `;` between them. The `;` after the last statement is optional. Extra `;` are ignored.

- When you send a text (with `kareladb sql`, a file, or HTTP `/exec`), KarelaDB first checks the **grammar** of the whole text. If one statement has a syntax error, **no** statement runs. (`kareladb shell` runs what you typed each time a line ends with `;`.)
- Then the statements run one by one. Each one is saved on its own.
- At the first error while running, KarelaDB **stops**. The statements before it stay saved. The statements after it do not run.
- One statement is all or nothing: an `INSERT` of 5000 rows with one bad row saves no row.
- **Notes:** to make many statements succeed or fail together, use [BEGIN ... COMMIT](transactions.md).

**Example: Three statements, one result each**

```sql
CREATE TABLE brokers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name STRING NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (58, 'Northgate Securities');;
SELECT id, name FROM brokers
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE brokers (`

```text
table 'brokers' created
```

`INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (58, 'Northgate Securities')`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT id, name FROM brokers`

| id (INT) | name (STRING) |
|---|---|
| 58 | Northgate Securities |

(1 row)

**Example: A script stops at the first error; row 21 stays saved** (shows an error)

Setup:

```sql
CREATE TABLE brokers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name STRING NOT NULL);
```

```sql
INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (21, 'Test Broker A');
INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (21, 'Test Broker B');
INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (22, 'Test Broker C');
```

Result:

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

Error: `a row with id='21' already exists in 'brokers'. Use INSERT OR REPLACE to overwrite it, or INSERT OR IGNORE to skip it`

**Example: A syntax error in the second statement: the first does not run either** (shows an error)

```sql
CREATE TABLE notes (id INT, body STRING);
SELEC * FROM notes;
```

Result:

Error: `line 2, column 1: expected a statement (CREATE, DROP, RENAME, ALTER, SHOW, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, BACKUP, CHECK, SELECT, EXPLAIN, CALL, BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT, DECLARE, FETCH or CLOSE) but found 'SELEC'`

<a id="case"></a>

## Upper and lower case

Syntax:

```sql
SELECT = select = Select
ochl_day = OCHL_DAY = Ochl_Day
'CITY' <> 'city'
```

Keywords, table names, column names and function names do not care about case. **Text values do**: `'CITY'` is not `'city'`.

- A table or column keeps the spelling you used in `CREATE TABLE`. `SHOW TABLES` shows that spelling.
- A column name in the result keeps the spelling of the alias you wrote.
- **Notes:** in PostgreSQL, a name in double quotes is case sensitive. In KarelaDB it is not: `"Total"` and `"total"` are the same name.

**Example: Any case works for names; text compares exactly**

```sql
CREATE TABLE Brokers (Id INT PRIMARY KEY, Name STRING);
INSERT INTO BROKERS (ID, NAME) VALUES (58, 'Northgate Securities');
select id, name, name = 'northgate securities' AS same_text, upper(name) = 'NORTHGATE SECURITIES' AS same_upper from brokers;
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE Brokers (`

```text
table 'Brokers' created
```

`INSERT INTO BROKERS (ID, NAME) VALUES (58, 'Northgate Securities')`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT id, name, name = 'northgate securities' AS same_text, upper(name) = 'NORTHGATE SECURITIES' AS`

| Id (INT) | Name (STRING) | same_text (BOOL) | same_upper (BOOL) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 58 | Northgate Securities | false | true |

(1 row)

<a id="names"></a>

## Names and "quoted names"

Syntax:

```sql
name
"any name"
"a name with a "" inside"
```

A **name** (also called identifier) names a table, column, alias, view or index. A plain name has letters, digits and `_`, and does not start with a digit. Letters of any language (Nepali, Chinese, ...) also work.

Write a name in **double quotes** when it:

- is a [reserved word](#reserved-words), like `"order"` or `"select"`;
- has a space or another special character, like `"Total Amount"`;
- starts with a digit, like `"1st_level"`.

| Part | Rule |
|---|---|
| Plain name | letters (any language), digits, `_`; not starting with a digit |
| Quoted name | any characters; a `"` inside is written twice: `""` |
| Empty name `""` | not allowed |

- **Notes:** `time`, `date`, `timestamp`, `symbol`, `partition`, `open`, `close`, `volume`, `value` and `key` are **not** reserved. Use them freely as column names.

**Example: A forum table with a column called order**

```sql
CREATE TABLE posts (id LONG PRIMARY KEY, "order" INT, "Posted By" STRING, body STRING);
INSERT INTO posts VALUES (1, 1, 'ram', 'First post');
SELECT id, "order", "Posted By" FROM posts ORDER BY "order";
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE posts (`

```text
table 'posts' created
```

`INSERT INTO posts VALUES (1, 1, 'ram', 'First post')`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT id, "order", "Posted By" FROM posts ORDER BY "order"`

| id (LONG) | order (INT) | Posted By (STRING) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | ram |

(1 row)

**Example: Names in any language work without quotes (here Nepali)**

```sql
CREATE TABLE कम्पनी (चिन्ह STRING PRIMARY KEY, नाम STRING);
INSERT INTO कम्पनी VALUES ('CITY', 'नमस्ते');
SELECT चिन्ह, नाम FROM कम्पनी;
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE कम्पनी (`

```text
table 'कम्पनी' created
```

`INSERT INTO कम्पनी VALUES ('CITY', 'नमस्ते')`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT चिन्ह, नाम FROM कम्पनी`

| चिन्ह (STRING) | नाम (STRING) |
|---|---|
| CITY | नमस्ते |

(1 row)

**Example: A reserved word without quotes** (shows an error)

```sql
CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, order STRING);
```

Result:

Error: `line 1, column 30: expected a column name but found the reserved word 'order' (write it in double quotes, "order", to use it as a name)`

<a id="text"></a>

## Text: 'single quotes'

Syntax:

```sql
'text'
'City''s bank'
''
```

Text (also called a string) goes in **single quotes**. A `'` inside the text is written twice: `''`. Text may have many lines and any language (UTF-8).

- There are no backslash escapes: `'a\nb'` is the four characters `a`, `\`, `n`, `b`.
- `''` is an empty text. It is **not** NULL.
- Double quotes `"..."` are for names, never for text. `WHERE symbol = "CITY"` looks for a **column** called CITY.
- **Notes:** bytes are written `X'0A0B'`; see [BYTES](column-types.md#bytes). Times are text too: `'2026-09-10T11:00:00+05:45'`; see [TIMESTAMP](column-types.md#timestamp).

**Example: Quotes inside text, empty text, text in another language**

```sql
SELECT 'City''s bank' AS name,
       '' AS empty, '' IS NULL AS empty_is_null,
       'नेपाल' AS nepali,
       'a\nb' AS no_escapes;
```

Result:

| name (STRING) | empty (STRING) | empty_is_null (BOOL) | nepali (STRING) | no_escapes (STRING) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| City's bank |  | false | नेपाल | a\\nb |

(1 row)

**Example: Double quotes mean a column name, not text** (shows an error)

```sql
CREATE TABLE securities (symbol SYMBOL PRIMARY KEY, name STRING);
SELECT name FROM securities WHERE symbol = "CITY";
```

Result:

```text
table 'securities' created
```

Error: `line 2, column 44: unknown column 'CITY' (table 'securities' has: symbol name)`

**Example: Text without its closing quote** (shows an error)

```sql
SELECT 'Northgate;
```

Result:

Error: `line 1, column 8: expected a closing ' to end the string that starts here but found the end of the input`

<a id="numbers"></a>

## Numbers

Syntax:

```sql
42    -7    512.45    .5    1.5e3    2E-4
```

A number without a point or `e` is a whole number (type `LONG`). A number with a point or `e` is a `DOUBLE`.

| Written | Type | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `42`, `-7` | `LONG` | -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807 |
| `512.45`, `.5`, `1.5e3` | `DOUBLE` | about ±1.8e308, 15 digits |

- There is no `,` or `_` inside a number: write `1000000`, not `1,000,000`.
- A number put into a column is converted to the column type; see [column types](column-types.md).
- `/` always gives a `DOUBLE`: `10 / 4` is `2.5`. See [arithmetic](functions-math.md#operators).
- **Notes:** for exact money, the column type matters, not the literal: use `DECIMAL(2)` columns. For amounts with more than about 15 digits, write the value as text: `'123456789012345.67'`.

**Example: Kinds of numbers**

```sql
SELECT 42 AS whole, -7 AS negative, 512.45 AS price, .5 AS half, 1.5e3 AS thousand_five, 2E-4 AS small, 10 / 4 AS division;
```

Result:

| whole (LONG) | negative (LONG) | price (DOUBLE) | half (DOUBLE) | thousand_five (DOUBLE) | small (DOUBLE) | division (DOUBLE) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 42 | -7 | 512.45 | 0.5 | 1500 | 0.0002 | 2.5 |

(1 row)

**Example: A whole number that is too big** (shows an error)

```sql
SELECT 9223372036854775808;
```

Result:

Error: `line 1, column 8: expected an integer between -9223372036854775808 and 9223372036854775807 but found '9223372036854775808'`

<a id="constants"></a>

## TRUE, FALSE and NULL

Syntax:

```sql
TRUE    FALSE    NULL
```

`TRUE` and `FALSE` are the two `BOOL` values. `NULL` means "no value" or "unknown". Every column type can hold `NULL`, unless the column is `NOT NULL`.

- `NULL` is not `0`, not `''` and not `FALSE`.
- Use `IS NULL` and `IS NOT NULL` to test for `NULL`. See [NULL logic](#null-logic).
- **Notes:** a `BOOL` is not a number: `TRUE = 1` is an error. A `BOOL` column accepts `1`/`0` and `'true'`/`'false'` when a row is written.

**Example: The three constants**

```sql
SELECT TRUE AS yes, FALSE AS no, NULL AS nothing, NULL IS NULL AS is_null, NOT FALSE AS not_false;
```

Result:

| yes (BOOL) | no (BOOL) | nothing (STRING) | is_null (BOOL) | not_false (BOOL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| true | false | NULL | true | true |

(1 row)

**Example: A user who has not verified the email yet**

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (id LONG PRIMARY KEY AUTO, email STRING NOT NULL, verified BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, phone STRING);
INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ('ram@example.com');
INSERT INTO users (email, verified, phone) VALUES ('sita@example.com', TRUE, '9800000000');
SELECT id, email, verified, phone, phone IS NULL AS no_phone FROM users;
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE users (`

```text
table 'users' created
```

`INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ('ram@example.com')`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`INSERT INTO users (email, verified, phone) VALUES ('sita@example.com', TRUE, '9800000000')`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT id, email, verified, phone, phone IS NULL AS no_phone FROM users`

| id (LONG) | email (STRING) | verified (BOOL) | phone (STRING) | no_phone (BOOL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ram@example.com | false | NULL | true |
| 2 | sita@example.com | true | 9800000000 | false |

(2 rows)

<a id="comments"></a>

## Comments

Syntax:

```sql
-- to the end of the line
/* between these marks, also over many lines */
```

KarelaDB skips comments. Use them to explain a script.

- `/* ... */` comments do not nest: the first `*/` ends the comment.
- A `/*` without `*/` is an error that shows where the comment starts.

**Example: Both kinds of comments in a report query**

Setup:

```sql
CREATE TABLE ledger (id LONG PRIMARY KEY AUTO, account INT, amount DECIMAL(2));
INSERT INTO ledger (account, amount) VALUES (1, 1000.00), (1, -250.50), (2, 250.50);
```

```sql
/* Balance per account.
   Used by the daily report. */
SELECT account,            -- the account number
       sum(amount) AS balance
FROM ledger
GROUP BY account
ORDER BY account;
```

Result:

| account (INT) | balance (DECIMAL(2)) |
|---|---|
| 1 | 749.50 |
| 2 | 250.50 |

(2 rows)

**Example: A comment that is not closed** (shows an error)

```sql
SELECT 1 /* forgot to close
```

Result:

Error: `line 1, column 10: expected '*/' to close the comment that starts here but found the end of the input`

<a id="errors"></a>

## Error messages

Syntax:

```sql
error: line L, column C: expected ... but found ...
error: <what is wrong>
```

When KarelaDB cannot run a statement, it prints `error:` and a message. Messages about the SQL text say **where**: `line 3, column 8` is the place in the text you sent (in a file: the line of the file). They also say what KarelaDB expected there.

| Message starts with | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `expected ... but found ...` | the grammar is wrong at that place |
| `unknown column 'x' (table 't' has: ...)` | a typing mistake; the message lists the real columns |
| `table or view 'x' does not exist` | wrong table name, or the wrong database |
| `a row with ... already exists` | a duplicate key; see [INSERT](insert.md#duplicates) |
| `column 'x' (TYPE): ...` | a value does not fit the column; see [column types](column-types.md) |

- **Returns:** exit code `1` from `kareladb sql`; HTTP status 400 from the HTTP API.
- **Notes:** a missing comma is not an error: `SELECT symbol close` means "column `symbol`, named `close`". [Chapter 12](../tutorial/12-troubleshooting.md) lists many messages and their fixes.

**Example: The message points to line 3, column 8** (shows an error)

Setup:

```sql
CREATE TABLE ochl_day (time TIMESTAMP, symbol SYMBOL, close DOUBLE) TIMESERIES(time);
```

```sql
SELECT time,
       symbol,
       clsoe
FROM ochl_day;
```

Result:

Error: `line 3, column 8: unknown column 'clsoe' (table 'ochl_day' has: time symbol close)`

**Example: What the grammar wanted** (shows an error)

Setup:

```sql
CREATE TABLE ochl_day (time TIMESTAMP, symbol SYMBOL, close DOUBLE) TIMESERIES(time);
```

```sql
SELECT symbol close FROM ochl_day WHERE;
```

Result:

Error: `line 1, column 40: expected an expression (a value, column name, function call or '(') but found ';'`

<a id="reserved-words"></a>

## Reserved words

Syntax:

```sql
ALTER AND AS BETWEEN CASE CREATE DEFAULT DELETE DISTINCT DROP ELSE END
FALSE FROM GROUP IN INSERT INTO IS JOIN LIKE LIMIT NOT NULL ON OR ORDER
PRIMARY REFERENCES SELECT SET TABLE THEN TO TRUE UNIQUE UPDATE VALUES WHEN WHERE
```

These 40 words have a fixed meaning. They cannot be a table, column or alias name, unless you write them in double quotes: `"order"`, `"from"`.

- All other words are normal names, also words like `CHECK`, `INDEX`, `BEGIN`, `KEY`, `USER`, `DATE`, `TIME`, `OPEN` and `CLOSE`: KarelaDB knows them from their place in the statement.
- **Notes:** PostgreSQL reserves more words. A name that works in KarelaDB may need quotes in PostgreSQL.

**Example: Columns called time, date, open, close, key and value need no quotes**

```sql
CREATE TABLE prices (time TIMESTAMP, date DATE, open DOUBLE, close DOUBLE, key STRING, value DOUBLE) TIMESERIES(time);
INSERT INTO prices VALUES ('2026-09-10', '2026-09-10', 504.6, 504.9, 'CITY', 1);
SELECT time, date, open, close, key, value FROM prices;
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE prices (`

```text
table 'prices' created
```

`INSERT INTO prices VALUES ('2026-09-10', '2026-09-10', 504.6, 504.9, 'CITY', 1)`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT time, date, open, close, key, value FROM prices`

| time (TIMESTAMP) | date (DATE) | open (DOUBLE) | close (DOUBLE) | key (STRING) | value (DOUBLE) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-10T00:00:00.000Z | 2026-09-10 | 504.6 | 504.9 | CITY | 1 |

(1 row)

**Example: A reserved word as a column name** (shows an error)

```sql
CREATE TABLE transfers (id INT, from INT, to_account INT);
```

Result:

Error: `line 1, column 33: expected a column name but found the reserved word 'from' (write it in double quotes, "from", to use it as a name)`

<a id="clause-words"></a>

## Clause words

Syntax:

```sql
ASOF CROSS FULL HAVING INNER LATEST LEFT LT OVER REFRESH RIGHT SAMPLE SPLICE UNION USING
```

These 15 words start a part of a query (a **clause**), like `LEFT JOIN` or `SAMPLE BY`. They **can** be table and column names. But they cannot be a short alias without `AS`: write `SELECT 1 AS left`, not `SELECT 1 left`.

| Word | Used in |
|---|---|
| `INNER`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `FULL`, `CROSS`, `USING` | [joins](joins.md) |
| `ASOF`, `LT`, `SPLICE` | [time joins](joins.md#asof-join) |
| `HAVING` | [GROUP BY](group-by.md) |
| `LATEST` | [LATEST ON](latest-on.md) |
| `SAMPLE` | [SAMPLE BY](sample-by.md) |
| `UNION` | [UNION ALL](union-subqueries.md) |
| `OVER` | [window functions](functions-window.md) |
| `REFRESH` | `CREATE CACHED VIEW ... REFRESH ON COMMIT` ([views](views.md)) |

**Example: Clause words as column names, and as aliases with AS**

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (left INT, right INT, sample INT, latest INT);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 2, 3, 4);
SELECT left, right, sample AS union, latest AS over FROM t;
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE t (`

```text
table 't' created
```

`INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 2, 3, 4)`

```text
1 row(s) inserted
```

`SELECT left, right, sample AS union, latest AS over FROM t`

| left (INT) | right (INT) | union (INT) | over (INT) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |

(1 row)

**Example: RIGHT JOIN: every broker, also the ones without trades**

Setup:

```sql
CREATE TABLE brokers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name STRING);
CREATE TABLE trades (id LONG PRIMARY KEY, buyer INT);
INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (1, 'Alpha'), (2, 'Beta');
INSERT INTO trades VALUES (10, 1);
```

```sql
SELECT brokers.name, trades.id FROM trades RIGHT JOIN brokers ON trades.buyer = brokers.id ORDER BY brokers.name;
```

Result:

| name (STRING) | id (LONG) |
|---|---|
| Alpha | 10 |
| Beta | NULL |

(2 rows)

**Example: A clause word as a short alias** (shows an error)

```sql
SELECT 1 left;
```

Result:

Error: `line 1, column 10: expected an operator, AS, ',', FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, UNION ALL, ORDER BY, LIMIT, ';' or the end of the input but found 'left'`

<a id="null-logic"></a>

## NULL logic

Syntax:

```sql
value IS NULL
value IS NOT NULL
NULL = anything   ->  NULL (unknown)
```

`NULL` means "unknown". So most things done with `NULL` give `NULL` again:

| Expression | Result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `NULL + 1` | `NULL` | unknown plus 1 is unknown |
| `NULL = NULL` | `NULL` | two unknown values may differ |
| `TRUE AND NULL` | `NULL` | depends on the unknown value |
| `FALSE AND NULL` | `FALSE` | false whatever the unknown value is |
| `TRUE OR NULL` | `TRUE` | true whatever the unknown value is |
| `NOT NULL` | `NULL` | |
| `3 IN (1, NULL)` | `NULL` | 3 might be the unknown value |
| `NULL IS NULL` | `TRUE` | the right way to test |

- `WHERE` and `HAVING` keep a row only when the condition is `TRUE`. A `NULL` condition drops the row, like `FALSE`.
- So `WHERE phone = NULL` finds nothing. Write `WHERE phone IS NULL`.
- `WHERE v <> 5` also drops the rows where `v` is `NULL`.
- Aggregates skip `NULL`: `count(v)` counts only values, `sum(v)` adds only values. `count(*)` counts all rows.
- `ORDER BY v` puts `NULL` last (with `DESC`: first).
- **Notes:** `coalesce(v, 0)` gives `0` for `NULL`; see [conditional functions](functions-conditional.md).

**Example: NULL in expressions**

```sql
SELECT NULL + 1 AS plus, NULL = NULL AS equal, TRUE AND NULL AS and_true, FALSE AND NULL AS and_false,
       TRUE OR NULL AS or_true, 3 IN (1, NULL) AS in_list, NULL IS NULL AS is_null;
```

Result:

| plus (STRING) | equal (STRING) | and_true (STRING) | and_false (BOOL) | or_true (BOOL) | in_list (STRING) | is_null (BOOL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NULL | NULL | NULL | false | true | NULL | true |

(1 row)

**Example: Users without a phone: = NULL finds nothing, IS NULL works**

Setup:

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (id INT PRIMARY KEY, email STRING, phone STRING);
INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'ram@example.com', NULL), (2, 'sita@example.com', '9800000000'), (3, 'hari@example.com', NULL);
```

```sql
SELECT id FROM users WHERE phone = NULL;
SELECT id FROM users WHERE phone IS NULL;
SELECT id FROM users WHERE phone <> '9800000000';
SELECT count(*) AS users, count(phone) AS with_phone FROM users;
```

Result:

`SELECT id FROM users WHERE phone = NULL`

| id (INT) |
|---|

(0 rows)

`SELECT id FROM users WHERE phone IS NULL`

| id (INT) |
|---|
| 1 |
| 3 |

(2 rows)

`SELECT id FROM users WHERE phone != '9800000000'`

| id (INT) |
|---|

(0 rows)

`SELECT count(*) AS users, count(phone) AS with_phone FROM users`

| users (LONG) | with_phone (LONG) |
|---|---|
| 3 | 1 |

(1 row)

# SQL command groups: DDL, DML, DCL, TCL, DQL

> The five groups of SQL statements, every KarelaDB statement in its group, and the role each group needs.

- Category: Getting started
- Keywords: DDL, DML, DCL, TCL, DQL, data definition language, data manipulation language, data control language, transaction control language, data query language, command groups, statement types, kinds of statements, sublanguage, which role do I need, TRUNCATE, SAVEPOINT
- See also: [SQL basics](sql-basics.md), [CREATE TABLE](create-table.md), [ALTER, RENAME and DROP TABLE](alter-table.md), [Views](views.md), [Indexes](indexes.md), [INSERT](insert.md), [UPDATE and DELETE](update-delete.md), [Users and roles](users-and-roles.md), [Transactions](transactions.md), [SELECT](select.md), [SHOW TABLES, COLUMNS, CREATE TABLE](show-tables.md)

SQL statements are sorted into five **groups** by what they do. The group tells you three things at once: what the statement changes, which [role](users-and-roles.md#roles) a user needs for it, and whether it can go inside [BEGIN ... COMMIT](transactions.md).

| Group | Name | What it does | Main statements | Role needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DDL** | Data Definition Language | makes, changes and removes **objects**: tables, views, indexes, functions, procedures, triggers | `CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`, `RENAME` | `admin` |
| **DML** | Data Manipulation Language | changes the **rows** inside tables | `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `CALL` | `write` |
| **DCL** | Data Control Language | says **who** may do what | `CREATE USER`, `GRANT`, `REVOKE` | `admin` as the user's own `ROLE` |
| **TCL** | Transaction Control Language | groups changes so they are saved **together or not at all** | `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK` | `read` |
| **DQL** | Data Query Language | **reads** rows and never changes anything | `SELECT`, `EXPLAIN`, `SHOW` | `read` |

- Roles are checked only by `kareladb serve` (HTTP, web console and the PostgreSQL port). `kareladb sql` and `kareladb shell` open the files directly and may run everything.
- Some books put `SELECT` into DML. KarelaDB's help keeps it apart as DQL, because a read needs only the `read` role.
- The web console lists what DDL made: open the **Objects** list on the left (see [web console](web-console.md#tables)).

<a id="ddl"></a>

## DDL: Data Definition Language

DDL statements build the **shape** of a database. They change objects, not rows (except `DROP`, which removes the rows with the table).

| Object | Make | Change | Remove | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| table | `CREATE TABLE` | `ALTER TABLE`, `RENAME TABLE` | `DROP TABLE`, then `UNDROP TABLE` to bring it back | [create-table](create-table.md), [alter-table](alter-table.md), [trash](trash.md) |
| view | `CREATE VIEW`, `CREATE CACHED VIEW` | drop and create again | `DROP VIEW` | [views](views.md) |
| materialized view | `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` | `ALTER TABLE ... SET TTL`; otherwise drop and create again | `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW` | [views](views.md#materialized-view) |
| index | `CREATE INDEX`, `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`, `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` | - | `DROP INDEX` | [indexes](indexes.md) |
| saved function | `CREATE FUNCTION` | `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` | `DROP FUNCTION` | [saved-functions](saved-functions.md) |
| stored procedure | `CREATE PROCEDURE` | `CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE` | `DROP PROCEDURE` | [procedures](procedures.md) |
| trigger | `CREATE TRIGGER` | `ALTER TRIGGER ... ENABLE / DISABLE` | `DROP TRIGGER` | [triggers](triggers.md) |
| sequence | `CREATE SEQUENCE` | `ALTER SEQUENCE` | `DROP SEQUENCE` | [functions-postgres](functions-postgres.md) |
| ENUM type | `CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM` | `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` | `DROP TYPE` | [column-types](column-types.md#enum) |
| trading calendar | `CREATE CALENDAR` | `ALTER CALENDAR ... ADD HOLIDAY` / `ADD ERA` / ... | `DROP CALENDAR` | [calendars](calendars.md) |
| database | `CREATE DATABASE` | `ALTER DATABASE` | `DROP DATABASE` | [databases](databases.md) |

- **Role:** `admin`. Databases need `admin` as the user's own `ROLE`.
- **Notes:**
  - Each DDL statement is saved on its own, at once. Most of them can not go inside `BEGIN` ... `COMMIT` (see [what is not allowed inside a transaction](transactions.md#not-inside)).
  - Look at what DDL made with `SHOW TABLES`, `SHOW COLUMNS FROM t`, `SHOW CREATE TABLE t`, `SHOW VIEWS`, `SHOW INDEXES`, `SHOW FUNCTIONS`, `SHOW PROCEDURES` and `SHOW TRIGGERS` (see [show-tables](show-tables.md)).
  - `TRUNCATE TABLE t` empties a table and keeps it (see [UPDATE and DELETE](update-delete.md#truncate)). PostgreSQL counts it as DDL.

**Example: DDL: a table, a column added later, a view and an index** (sample data: sample)

```sql
CREATE TABLE watchlist (symbol STRING PRIMARY KEY, note STRING);
ALTER TABLE watchlist ADD COLUMN target DOUBLE;
CREATE VIEW watchlist_names AS
SELECT w.symbol, s.name, w.target FROM watchlist w JOIN securities s ON s.symbol = w.symbol;
CREATE INDEX watchlist_note ON watchlist (note);
SHOW COLUMNS FROM watchlist;
SHOW VIEWS;
```

Result:

`CREATE TABLE watchlist (`

```text
table 'watchlist' created
```

`ALTER TABLE watchlist ADD COLUMN target DOUBLE`

```text
table 'watchlist' altered
```

`CREATE VIEW watchlist_names AS SELECT w.symbol, s.name, w.target FROM watchlist AS w JOIN securities`

```text
view 'watchlist_names' created
```

`CREATE INDEX watchlist_note ON watchlist (note)`

```text
index 'watchlist_note' created on table 'watchlist' (0 rows)
```

`SHOW COLUMNS FROM watchlist`

| name (STRING) | type (STRING) | primary_key (BOOL) | not_null (BOOL) | computed (BOOL) | references (STRING) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| symbol | STRING | true | false | false | NULL |
| note | STRING | false | false | false | NULL |
| target | DOUBLE | false | false | false | NULL |

(3 rows)

`SHOW VIEWS`

| name (STRING) | query (STRING) | kind (STRING) | refresh (STRING) |
|---|---|---|---|
| watchlist_names | SELECT w.symbol, s.name, w.target FROM watchlist AS w JOIN securities AS s ON s.symbol = w.symbol | complex | NULL |

(1 row)

<a id="dml"></a>

## DML: Data Manipulation Language

DML statements change the **rows** of tables. The table itself stays as it is.

| Statement | What it does | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `INSERT INTO ... VALUES` | adds rows | [insert](insert.md) |
| `INSERT OR REPLACE`, `INSERT OR IGNORE`, `ON CONFLICT` | adds rows, or replaces / keeps the row with the same key | [insert](insert.md#insert-or-replace) |
| `INSERT INTO ... SELECT` | adds the rows a query gives | [insert](insert.md#insert-select) |
| `UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE` | changes rows | [update-delete](update-delete.md#update) |
| `DELETE FROM ... WHERE` | removes rows | [update-delete](update-delete.md#delete) |
| `... RETURNING` | shows the rows that were added, changed or removed | [update-delete](update-delete.md#returning) |
| `CALL name(...)` | runs a stored procedure, which changes rows | [procedures](procedures.md) |

- **Role:** `write`.
- **Notes:**
  - Each statement is all or nothing: an `INSERT` of 5000 rows with one bad row saves no row.
  - To make **many** DML statements succeed or fail together, put them inside `BEGIN` ... `COMMIT` (TCL).
  - Triggers run by themselves after (or before) DML on their table.
  - A view has no rows of its own: DML on a view is refused. Change the table the view reads.

**Example: DML: add, change and remove rows** (sample data: sample)

Setup:

```sql
CREATE TABLE watchlist (symbol STRING PRIMARY KEY, note STRING, target DOUBLE);
```

```sql
INSERT INTO watchlist VALUES ('CITY', 'bank', 520), ('VOLT', 'hydro', 250);
UPDATE watchlist SET target = 540 WHERE symbol = 'CITY';
DELETE FROM watchlist WHERE symbol = 'VOLT' RETURNING symbol, note;
SELECT * FROM watchlist;
```

Result:

`INSERT INTO watchlist VALUES ('CITY', 'bank', 520), ('VOLT', 'hydro', 250)`

```text
2 row(s) inserted
```

`UPDATE watchlist SET target = 540 WHERE symbol = 'CITY'`

```text
1 row(s) updated
```

`DELETE FROM watchlist WHERE symbol = 'VOLT' RETURNING symbol, note`

| symbol (STRING) | note (STRING) |
|---|---|
| VOLT | hydro |

(1 row)

```text
1 row(s) deleted
```

`SELECT * FROM watchlist`

| symbol (STRING) | note (STRING) | target (DOUBLE) |
|---|---|---|
| CITY | bank | 540 |

(1 row)

<a id="dcl"></a>

## DCL: Data Control Language

DCL statements decide **who** may connect and what each user may do.

| Statement | What it does | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `CREATE USER name PASSWORD '...' ROLE ...` | adds a user with a role for every database | [users-and-roles](users-and-roles.md#create-user) |
| `ALTER USER` | changes a password or a role | [users-and-roles](users-and-roles.md#alter-user) |
| `DROP USER` | removes a user | [users-and-roles](users-and-roles.md#drop-user) |
| `GRANT role ON DATABASE db TO name` | gives a role on one database | [users-and-roles](users-and-roles.md#grant) |
| `GRANT ... ON TABLE` | gives rights on one table | [table-rights](table-rights.md) |
| `REVOKE ... FROM name` | takes a grant away | [users-and-roles](users-and-roles.md#revoke) |
| `SHOW USERS` | lists users, roles and grants | [users-and-roles](users-and-roles.md#show-users) |

The roles, from least to most: `none` < `read` < `write` < `admin`. Each role may do everything of the roles before it.

- **Role:** `admin` as the user's **own** `ROLE` (a `GRANT` of admin on one database is not enough), because users belong to the whole server. Changing your own password needs no role.
- **Notes:**
  - The **first** user must have `ROLE admin`. From then on, `kareladb serve` asks everyone to log in.
  - Users are kept in the `_system` database, not in the database you are using.
  - Give each program only what it needs: an app's backend `write` on its own database, a report script `read`.

**Example: DCL: an admin, a read-only report user, and an app that may write one database** (sample data: sample)

Setup:

```sql
CREATE USER admin WITH PASSWORD 'Long-Admin-Passw0rd' ROLE admin;
```

```sql
CREATE USER report WITH PASSWORD 'Reports-only-secret-7' ROLE read;
CREATE USER shop_app WITH PASSWORD 'Another-long-secret-42' ROLE none;
GRANT write ON DATABASE demo TO shop_app;
SHOW USERS;
```

Result:

`CREATE USER report WITH PASSWORD '***' ROLE read`

```text
user 'report' created with role read
```

`CREATE USER shop_app WITH PASSWORD '***' ROLE none`

```text
user 'shop_app' created with role none
```

`GRANT write ON DATABASE demo TO shop_app`

```text
user 'shop_app' has role write on database 'demo'
```

`SHOW USERS`

| name (STRING) | role (STRING) | grants (STRING) | created (TIMESTAMP) | changed (TIMESTAMP) | table_grants (STRING) | two_factor (BOOL) | statement_timeout (STRING) | priority (STRING) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| admin | admin | NULL | 2026-10-24T06:19:36.201Z | 2026-10-24T06:19:36.201Z | NULL | false | NULL | NULL |
| report | read | NULL | 2026-10-24T06:19:36.376Z | 2026-10-24T06:19:36.376Z | NULL | false | NULL | NULL |
| shop_app | none | demo=write | 2026-10-24T06:19:36.433Z | 2026-10-24T06:19:36.436Z | NULL | false | NULL | NULL |

(3 rows)

<a id="tcl"></a>

## TCL: Transaction Control Language

TCL statements group DML into one **transaction**: KarelaDB saves all of its changes together, or none of them.

| Statement | What it does | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `BEGIN` (also `BEGIN TRANSACTION`, `BEGIN WORK`) | starts a transaction | [transactions](transactions.md#begin) |
| `COMMIT` | saves every change since `BEGIN`, in one write | [transactions](transactions.md#commit) |
| `ROLLBACK` | throws away every change since `BEGIN` | [transactions](transactions.md#rollback) |
| `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` | reads rows that no other session may change before you `COMMIT` | [transactions](transactions.md#for-update) |

- **Role:** `read` to start and end one. The statements inside still need their own role (`write` for DML).
- **Notes:**
  - Without `BEGIN`, every statement is its own small transaction and is saved at once.
  - When a statement inside the transaction fails, KarelaDB undoes the whole transaction.
  - `SAVEPOINT`, `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` and `RELEASE SAVEPOINT` undo part of a transaction ([savepoints](transactions.md#savepoint)).
  - One writer at a time: while a transaction changes rows, other writers wait (see [one writer at a time](transactions.md#one-writer)).

**Example: TCL: a transfer that is saved, and a mistake that is undone** (sample data: sample)

Setup:

```sql
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INT PRIMARY KEY, owner STRING NOT NULL, balance DECIMAL(2) NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO accounts VALUES (1, 'Ram', 1000), (2, 'Sita', 0);
```

```sql
BEGIN;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 300 WHERE id = 1;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 300 WHERE id = 2;
COMMIT;

BEGIN;
DELETE FROM accounts;
ROLLBACK;

SELECT * FROM accounts ORDER BY id;
```

Result:

`BEGIN`

```text
transaction started
```

`UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 300 WHERE id = 1`

```text
1 row(s) updated
```

`UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 300 WHERE id = 2`

```text
1 row(s) updated
```

`COMMIT`

```text
transaction committed: 2 change(s) saved
```

`BEGIN`

```text
transaction started
```

`DELETE FROM accounts`

```text
2 row(s) deleted
```

`ROLLBACK`

```text
transaction rolled back: 1 change(s) undone
```

`SELECT * FROM accounts ORDER BY id`

| id (INT) | owner (STRING) | balance (DECIMAL(2)) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ram | 700.00 |
| 2 | Sita | 300.00 |

(2 rows)

<a id="dql"></a>

## DQL: Data Query Language

DQL statements **read**. They never change a row or an object, so they are safe to run at any time.

| Statement | What it does | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `SELECT` | reads rows: `WHERE`, `JOIN`, `GROUP BY`, `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT` | [select](select.md) |
| `SELECT ... SAMPLE BY`, `LATEST ON` | time-series candles and the newest row per key | [sample-by](sample-by.md), [latest-on](latest-on.md) |
| `WITH ... SELECT` | a query with named parts | [union-subqueries](union-subqueries.md) |
| `EXPLAIN SELECT ...` | shows how KarelaDB will run a query, without running it | [explain](explain.md) |
| `SHOW TABLES`, `SHOW VIEWS`, `SHOW INDEXES`, ... | lists the objects of a database | [show-tables](show-tables.md) |
| `DECLARE`, `FETCH`, `CLOSE` | reads a big result a part at a time | [cursors](cursors.md) |

- **Role:** `read`.
- **Notes:**
  - Selecting from a view is DQL too: the view's query runs, and nothing is changed.
  - `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` is the one read that waits for writers; it belongs with TCL.

**Example: DQL: a report, a query plan and a list of objects** (sample data: sample)

```sql
SELECT symbol, count(*) AS trades, sum(quantity) AS shares
FROM trade_log GROUP BY symbol ORDER BY trades DESC, symbol LIMIT 3;
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM ochl_day WHERE symbol = 'CITY';
SHOW TABLES;
```

Result:

`SELECT symbol, count(*) AS trades, sum(quantity) AS shares FROM trade_log GROUP BY symbol ORDER BY t`

| symbol (SYMBOL) | trades (LONG) | shares (LONG) |
|---|---|---|
| CITY | 11 | 2420 |
| COAST | 11 | 3070 |
| TELCO | 6 | 2770 |

(3 rows)

`EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM ochl_day WHERE symbol = 'CITY'`

| plan (STRING) |
|---|
| scan table ochl_day (2 of 2 partitions, about 57 rows) |
| read only 1 key range(s) of each partition |
| filter while scanning: 1 condition(s) |
| engine: column |

(4 rows)

`SHOW TABLES`

| name (STRING) | kind (STRING) | partition (STRING) | columns (INT) | rows (LONG) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| brokers | relational | NONE | 2 | 5 |
| live_data | timeseries | DAY | 12 | 12 |
| ochl_day | timeseries | YEAR | 7 | 57 |
| ochl_minutes | timeseries | MONTH | 7 | 956 |
| securities | relational | NONE | 3 | 5 |
| trade_log | timeseries | DAY | 8 | 32 |

(6 rows)

<a id="which-group"></a>

## Which group is my statement?

| Starts with | Group |
|---|---|
| `CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`, `RENAME`, `UNDROP` (tables, views, indexes, functions, procedures, triggers, sequences, databases) | DDL |
| `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `CALL` | DML |
| `CREATE USER`, `ALTER USER`, `DROP USER`, `GRANT`, `REVOKE` | DCL |
| `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK` | TCL |
| `SELECT`, `WITH`, `EXPLAIN`, `SHOW`, `DECLARE`, `FETCH`, `CLOSE` | DQL |

Other statements belong to looking after the database, not to one of the five groups: `BACKUP DATABASE`, `CHECK TABLE`, `CHECKPOINT` (see [backup and safety](backup-and-safety.md)) and `USE` (see [databases](databases.md#use)).
