# 6. Web console

- Category: Tutorial

## What you will learn

- How to start the server and open the console in a browser.
- Every part of the console screen: the Home menu, database list, objects, editor, results grid, chart, terminal and the panels on the right (Monitor, Health, Samples, Databases, Tools).
- How to use an access token, and how to keep the server safe.

## Start the server

```powershell
kareladb serve market --backups backups
```

```text
KarelaDB 0.2.0-dev
  console   http://127.0.0.1:9900
  postgres  127.0.0.1:8832 (PostgreSQL protocol, no TLS; no password on this computer only)
  data      market
  backups   backups
  access    no token
  commits   synced to disk before they are confirmed (--sync-commits always)
  limits    statement timeout 1 min, result memory 1.00 GB, 5000000 groups, 32 statements per user
  safety    writes allowed; DROP TABLE kept 7 days (UNDROP TABLE); audit log off
  recovery  manifest copy: b, last shutdown: clean

Press Ctrl+C to stop.
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:9900> in Chrome, Edge or Firefox. While the server runs, it prints one line per request, for example `2026-09-11 14:07:33  GET /health 200 0 ms`.

`kareladb serve market` serves **one** database folder (here the folder `market`). To serve **every database in the data folder** (chapter 1), start it without a folder:

```powershell
kareladb serve --backups backups
```

```text
KarelaDB 0.2.0-dev
  console   http://127.0.0.1:9900
  postgres  127.0.0.1:8832 (PostgreSQL protocol, no TLS; no password on this computer only)
  data      D:/AMP/TechnivsProject/01_NChartPro/KDB/build/bin/data (from program folder; one folder per database)
  default   default (used when a request names no database)
  backups   backups/<database name>
  access    no token
  commits   synced to disk before they are confirmed (--sync-commits always)
  limits    statement timeout 1 min, result memory 1.00 GB, 5000000 groups, 32 statements per user
  safety    writes allowed; DROP TABLE kept 7 days (UNDROP TABLE); audit log on (SHOW AUDIT)
  recovery  the default database is created when it is first used

Press Ctrl+C to stop.
```

Then the console can switch between databases and create new ones (see [Databases](#databases) below). Each database backs up into its own sub-folder of the backup folder, so backups never mix.

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir FOLDER` | The data folder to serve (without a database folder argument) | `KARELADB_DATA_DIR`, else `data` next to `kareladb.exe` |
| `--db NAME` | The database used when a request names none. In the data folder it is created when first used. | `default` (or the name you gave) |
| `--port N` | TCP port | `9900` |
| `--bind ADDRESS` | Which network address to listen on. `127.0.0.1` = this computer only. `0.0.0.0` = all networks. | `127.0.0.1` |
| `--backups FOLDER` | Backup folder. Needed for the **Backup now** button and `BACKUP DATABASE`. Also used by repairs. | not set |
| `--token SECRET` | Every request needs this token (see below). | no token |
| `--memory MB` | Memory for table data kept loaded. Data over this is read from disk again when needed, which is slower. On a PC or VPS with years of market history (about 1.5 GB on disk), `--memory 4096` keeps queries fast. | `512` |

- **Stop the server with Ctrl+C.** KarelaDB then closes the database cleanly (`database closed cleanly`).
- If the window is closed or the process is killed, nothing committed is lost. The next start replays the log and shows `last shutdown: not clean (crash or kill)`.
- Only one server (or other `kareladb` command) can use a database folder at a time.

To check from PowerShell that the page is there:

```powershell
$page = Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:9900/ -UseBasicParsing
"HTTP $($page.StatusCode), $($page.Headers['Content-Type'])"
if ($page.Content -match '<title>(.*?)</title>') { "title: $($Matches[1])" }
```

```text
HTTP 200, text/html; charset=utf-8
title: KarelaDB console
```

The console needs no internet. Its files are plain files in the folder `web` next to `kareladb` (in a source checkout: `web/console`). Chapter 1 lists where KarelaDB looks. A new console needs only the files copied, not a new program. When KarelaDB finds no console files, the page says so and lists the folders it looked in.

## The screen

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| KarelaDB [Home v]  Database [market v] New database   market v0.2.0-dev  * Connected  Help      |  <- top bar
+-----------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+--------+
| OBJECTS       Refresh | [Run Ctrl+Enter] [Run all Ctrl+Shift+Enter] [History]  Rows | Monitor|
| [Tables 6][Views][Trig]|  1  SELECT time, open, high, low, close, volume          | Health |  <- right side
| [Procs][Funcs][Timers] |  2  FROM ochl_day WHERE symbol = 'CITY';                | Samples|
|  > brokers     REL    | Error  line 2, column 8  unknown column ...               | Databa.|
|  > ochl_day    TS     |========================= (drag) ============================| Tools  |
|  ...                  | [1 SELECT time, ...] [2 Error]                           | ------ |
|  > Indexes            | [Grid][Chart]  message                      [Export CSV] |Terminal|
|                       |  #  time                      open   high ...            |        |
|                       |========================= (drag) ============================|        |
|                       | TERMINAL [All][Queries][Writes][Timers][Errors]  Pause Clear x|        |
|                       | 14:19:02.114 HTTP 127.0.0.1  market  3 ms  2 rows  SELECT ... |        |
+-----------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+--------+
| 19 rows | parse 0.05 ms  execute 0.34 ms  round trip 12 ms           Server 2026-09-11 14:19 |  <- status bar
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

The lines between the editor, the results and the terminal can be dragged. The console remembers the sizes.

### Top bar

| Part | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Home** menu | The pages: **Home** (this page: editor, grid, chart), **Dashboard** (many charts on one page, chapter 20), **View data** (browse tables and change rows with forms), **Keep data** (how long each table keeps its rows), **Settings** (where the data is kept, and who may log in). The button shows where you are, for example `Home / Dashboard`. |
| **Database** list | The database everything on the page uses: editor, object lists, health, timers, backups. See [Databases](#databases). |
| **New database** | Creates a database in the server's data folder. Only shown when the server serves a data folder. |
| Folder name, version | The folder of the chosen database, and the KarelaDB version |
| User and **Log out** | Only when the data folder has users (see [Login](#login-users)) |
| Connection dot | `Connected`, `Offline` (the server does not answer), `Token required` or `Login required` |
| **Help** | The help pages, the tutorial, keyboard shortcuts. Press **F1** on a word in the editor to open its help page. |
| Light / Dark button | Changes the colors. The browser remembers your choice. |

### Right side: Monitor, Health, Samples, Databases, Tools, Terminal

The buttons down the right side open a **panel** over the page. The same button closes it again; so do the **x** and `Esc`. The **pin** keeps a panel open beside the page. Drag its left edge to make it wider.

| Button | The panel |
|---|---|
| **Monitor** | Memory, processor, caches and the statements running now. **Cancel** stops a statement that was sent with a request id (chapter 8). |
| **Health** | Damaged files, backups, **Check now** and **Backup now** ([Health](#health-panel)). The button gets a red dot while a file is damaged. |
| **Samples** | Ready statements with **Insert** and **Run**. It opens by itself on your first visit. |
| **Databases** | Every database with its tables, size and folder. Click one to use it. **New database** and **Delete**. |
| **Tools** | **Purge trash** frees disk space in the whole data folder. **Delete all data** empties every table of the chosen database, after you type its name. |
| **Terminal** | Not a panel: shows or hides the terminal at the bottom of Home. |

### Terminal

The **terminal** under the results is a live log of what the server does: every statement, write, timer run, login and backup, from the console, from programs over HTTP, and from the PostgreSQL port.

- It is hidden when the page opens. It shows up by itself when you **Run** a statement. The **Terminal** button shows or hides it at any time, and counts the new lines while it is hidden.
- **All**, **Queries**, **Writes**, **Timers**, **Errors** show only that kind of line. A filter box keeps only lines with your text.
- Click a line to see all of its text. Double-click a statement to put it into the editor. Failed lines are red.
- Users who are not admins see only their own lines. The server keeps the last 5,000 events in memory (`--activity-log-size`).

### Databases

- The **Database** list at the top shows every database the server has. Pick one: the object lists and the health panel reload, and every statement you run goes to that database (the console adds `db=<name>` to each request, chapter 8).
- The browser **remembers** your choice. If that database is gone, the console uses the server's default database.
- **New database** asks for a name (letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64). Wrong names are refused at once. The new database is chosen right away and is empty.
- **Delete** next to a database in the **Databases** panel (right-hand rail) drops it. You type its name to confirm. Only a server admin sees the button. Like `DROP DATABASE`, it moves the folder to `_trash` in the data folder, and it is refused while a request or shell still uses the database.
- `USE demo;` in the editor also switches the list to `demo`.
- `CREATE DATABASE x;` and `DROP DATABASE x;` in the editor work too; the list reloads after them. If you drop the chosen database, the console goes back to the default database. `DROP DATABASE` never deletes data: the folder moves to `_trash` in the data folder.
- With `kareladb serve market` (one folder), the list has just that database and there is no **New database** button.

The list comes from `GET /api/databases`:

```powershell
$d = Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:9900/api/databases
"default: $($d.default)   can_create: $($d.can_create)"
$d.databases | Select-Object name, tables, default | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

```text
default: market  can_create: False

name  tables default
----  ------ -------
market     6    True
```

### Objects (left side)

The left side has one tab for each kind of object: **Tables**, **Views**, **Triggers**, **Procedures**, **Functions** and **Timers**. Each tab shows how many there are. Indexes are in the Tables tab, under the tables.

- Click the small arrow of a view, trigger, procedure or function to see its statement. **Open in editor** puts it into the editor.
- **Timers** run SQL by themselves on a schedule, for example `CALL refresh_prices();` every 5 minutes. **New timer** opens a form. The server runs them, also when no browser is open.
- **+ Folder** makes a folder, and you drag objects onto it. Folders only tidy this list. They are kept in the table `_console_groups`, so every browser sees them.

In the Tables tab:

- Every table with a badge: `TS` = time-series, `REL` = relational, and the partition (`DAY`, `MONTH`, `YEAR`).
- Click the small arrow to see the columns with their types. Marks: `TS` = time column, `PK` = primary key, `FK` = REFERENCES, `FX` = computed column.
- **Click** a table or column name: its name is put into the editor at the cursor.
- **Double-click** a table name: runs `SHOW COLUMNS FROM <table>`.
- **Refresh** reloads the lists and the health panel. They also reload by themselves after `CREATE`, `DROP`, `ALTER` or `RENAME`, and every 30 seconds.

### Editor

- Type SQL. Keywords, text and numbers get colors. Line numbers are on the left.
- The text stays in your browser. It is still there when you open the console again.
- `Tab` puts in two spaces.
- **Rows** (top right) is the most rows a query returns: 1,000 to 1,000,000. When a result is cut, the console says `Row limit reached`.

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Keys | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+Enter` | Run the statement under the cursor. If you selected text, run only the selection. |
| `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` | Run everything in the editor |
| `Tab` | Insert two spaces |
| `Escape` | Close the History list, or the open panel |
| `F1` | Open the help page of the word under the cursor |
| `Ctrl+C` (in the grid) | Copy the selected cell |
| Mac | Use `Cmd` instead of `Ctrl` |

### Running statements

- Statements are split at `;`. "The statement under the cursor" is the one between the `;` before and after the cursor.
- With many statements, each result gets a **tab** above the results (`1 SELECT ...`, `2 ...`).
- If a statement fails, a red **error bar** appears under the editor. The position (`line 2, column 8`) is counted in **your editor**, and the line is marked red. Click the position to jump there.
- The statements before the error ran and are saved. The error tab says so: `Before it: 1 statement(s) ran and are kept`.
- Statements like INSERT show a message (`3 row(s) inserted`) and the rows affected.

### History

**History** lists the last 50 statements you ran, newest first, with the time. Click one to put it back into the editor. The history is kept in this browser only.

### Grid

The grid shows the rows of a result.

- The column header shows the name and the type (`DOUBLE`, `TIMESTAMP`, ...). Numbers are right-aligned.
- **Click a header** to sort: first click small-to-big, second click big-to-small, third click back to the original order. Sorting happens in the browser, on the rows already loaded.
- **Drag the right edge** of a header to change the column width.
- **Click a cell** to select it. `Ctrl+C` or **double-click** copies its value.
- Empty values show as `null`. Long text shows fully when you hover over it.
- The grid is fast also with many rows: it only draws the rows you can see.

### Chart

Click **Chart** above the result. The chart button works when the result has a number column. KarelaDB picks the chart from the columns, for example:

- a `TIMESTAMP` or `DATE` column and columns named `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`: **candles**, with bars for a `volume` column;
- a time column and other numbers: **lines**;
- a text column and a number: **bars**; one row of numbers: a big **KPI number**.

Change the chart with the chart type list above the chart: line, area, bars, pie, donut, treemap, heatmaps, histogram, box plot, scatter, gauge, table and more. **Columns** chooses the columns, **Indicators** adds SMA, EMA, Bollinger, RSI, MACD or stochastic. **Chapter 20 explains every chart type and the dashboards.**

If the result has a SYMBOL or STRING column with more than one value (for example many symbols), a **symbol list** appears. The chart shows one symbol at a time (lines with up to 8 symbols get one line per symbol).

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| Mouse wheel | Zoom in and out around the mouse |
| Drag (hold the left button) | Move left and right |
| Double-click | Reset the view (candles: the last 200 bars) |
| Move the mouse | Crosshair. The top line shows date, O, H, L, C, change % and volume of that candle. The price and the date are marked on the axes. |
| Click a name in the legend | Hide or show that line |
| Arrow keys, `+`, `-`, `Home` (click the chart or press Tab first) | Move from candle to candle, zoom, reset |

- Candles have no gaps for days without trading (Friday, Saturday, holidays): each bar is one row. Untick **No gaps** to see real time.
- Times on the chart axis are shown in **your computer's time zone** (Nepal time on a PC set to Nepal). The grid shows UTC.
- Good queries for the chart: `SELECT time, open, high, low, close, volume FROM ochl_day WHERE symbol = 'CITY'`, or the candle queries of chapter 5.

### Export CSV

**Export CSV** downloads all rows of the result as a CSV file. It runs the statement **again** on the server (up to 1,000,000 rows), so it is only offered for `SELECT`, `SHOW` and `EXPLAIN`. The file name comes from the table name, for example `ochl_day.csv`. Times are UTC in ISO format.

### Health panel

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `OK - no damaged files` (green) / `DAMAGED (n)` (red) | Damaged files that KarelaDB knows about, with their names |
| Last backup | How long ago (`just now`, `3 h ago`), `never`, or `no backup folder` |
| Data | Size of the data files and how many |
| Log LSN | Number of the last change in the log. It grows with every change. |
| Opened | When the server opened the database |
| Recovery at open | What KarelaDB did when it opened the database. It opens by itself if there was a problem. |
| **Check now** | Reads every block of every file and the log. Example message: `OK: 11 files (76.1 KB) and 1 log segments read in 1.50 ms. No damage.` |
| **Backup now** | Makes a verified backup into the `--backups` folder. Example message: `Backup 20260911-083519-806 created and verified: 9 files, 222.3 KB.` The button is off when the server has no backup folder. |

If **Check now** finds damage, stop the server and run `kareladb repair` (chapter 9).

### Status bar (bottom)

- Left: the number of rows, and the times: `parse` and `execute` on the server, `round trip` including the network.
- Right: the server's clock, in your local time zone.

## Login (users)

When the data folder has users (chapter 16), the console shows **Log in** instead of the token box. Type the user name and password. After the login the top bar shows the user and role, for example `boss (admin)`, and a **Log out** button. The top bar dot says `Login required` while nobody is logged in.

- The login is kept in a cookie that scripts cannot read (`HttpOnly`) and that works only on this site (`SameSite=Strict`). It ends after 12 hours, at **Log out**, when the server restarts, or when the password changes.
- A wrong password keeps the form open with `Wrong user name or password.` After 5 wrong tries, wait a moment before the next one.
- Each statement runs with the user's role. A refused statement shows the error, for example `INSERT needs role write on database 'shop'; user 'report' has read`.
- The history of the editor never keeps passwords: `PASSWORD 'secret'` and the text in `password_hash('...')` are saved as `'***'`.

## Access token

Start the server with a token:

```powershell
kareladb serve market --token change-me-please
```

- The console asks for the token once (**Access token required**). The browser keeps it (local storage and a cookie for this site only).
- Programs send it in a header: `Authorization: Bearer change-me-please` (chapter 8).
- A wrong or missing token gets HTTP 401.
- `/health` works without a token. It only says `auth_required: true`.

Choose a long random token, for example:

```powershell
[Convert]::ToBase64String((1..24 | ForEach-Object { Get-Random -Maximum 256 }) -as [byte[]])
```

## Security notes

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| Only you, on this PC | Default (`--bind 127.0.0.1`, no token) is fine. |
| Other PCs in the office must connect | `--bind 0.0.0.0 --token <long secret>`. Open the port only in the Windows firewall for your office network. |
| Access over the internet | Do **not** open port 9900 to the internet. Put a reverse proxy with HTTPS (for example nginx or Caddy) in front, keep `--bind 127.0.0.1`, and use `--token`. |

What KarelaDB does to protect you:

- Without a token, KarelaDB listens on `127.0.0.1` only. If you use `--bind 0.0.0.0` **without** a token, the server prints a big **WARNING**: anyone who can reach the port can read, change and delete all data.
- The HTTP API refuses requests from other web sites (HTTP 403 `cross-site requests are not allowed`), so a bad web page in your browser cannot use your local KarelaDB.
- Without a token, the server only accepts the host names `localhost` and `127.x.x.x` (HTTP 403 otherwise). This stops "DNS rebinding" attacks. A reverse proxy that changes the `Host` header therefore needs `--token`.
- `GET /exec` only runs statements that read. Changes must use `POST` (chapter 8).
- There is **no HTTPS** inside KarelaDB. Use a reverse proxy.
- The token gives full access: everyone with the token can change and delete data. For people and programs that should do less, make **users** with roles instead (chapter 16).

## Try it yourself

1. Start the server with a backup folder. Make a backup with the button. Open the **Health** panel on the right.
2. Run the weekly candle query from chapter 5 for VOLT and look at it as a chart. Zoom in, then double-click.
3. Run `SELECT clsoe FROM ochl_day;` on line 3 of the editor. Which position does the error bar show?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. `kareladb serve market --backups backups`, then **Backup now**. "Last backup" changes to `just now`.
2. ```sql
   SELECT time, first(open) AS open, max(high) AS high, min(low) AS low, last(close) AS close, sum(volume) AS volume
   FROM ochl_day WHERE symbol = 'VOLT' SAMPLE BY 1w WEEK START SUNDAY;
   ```
   Then click **Chart**.
3. `line 3, column 8`. The console counts lines in your editor, not in the statement.

</details>

# 7. Command line and scripts

- Category: Tutorial

## What you will learn

- When a command means a database in the data folder, and when a folder path.
- The three output formats of `kareladb sql`: table, CSV and JSON.
- How to use KarelaDB in PowerShell and bash scripts (loops, exit codes, UTF-8 text).
- How to make a daily backup task with Windows Task Scheduler.

The examples use the database `market` with the sample data.

## Database names and folder paths

Every command that needs a database (`sql`, `shell`, `serve`, `info`, `check`, `repair`, `backup`) takes a **name** or a **path**:

| You write | KarelaDB uses |
|---|---|
| A name (only letters, digits, `_`, `-`), and the data folder has a database with that name | That database in the data folder (chapter 1). Upper or lower case does not matter. |
| A name, and the data folder has no database with that name | The folder with that name in the current folder, like before. It is created if it does not exist. |
| A path (it has `\`, `/`, `:` or `.`): `.\market`, `D:\kdb\market` | Always that folder |
| Nothing (`kareladb shell`, `kareladb serve`) | The data folder: the database `default` for the shell; all databases for the server |

- To be sure you mean the folder in the current folder, write `.\market` (Linux: `./market`).
- To make a database in the data folder, use `CREATE DATABASE` in `kareladb shell` (or in the console, or over HTTP).
- With a **name**, `kareladb backup` and `kareladb repair --backups` use the sub-folder `<backups-dir>\<name>`, the same place `kareladb serve` uses. With a path, they use `<backups-dir>` as before.

```powershell
$env:KARELADB_DATA_DIR = "kdb-data"

# Make a database in the data folder (kareladb shell runs CREATE DATABASE).
"CREATE DATABASE reports;" | kareladb shell | Out-Null

# A name that is in the data folder means that database, from any folder.
kareladb sql reports "CREATE TABLE daily (day DATE PRIMARY KEY, trades LONG); INSERT INTO daily VALUES ('2026-09-10', 32)"
kareladb sql reports "SELECT * FROM daily"
kareladb info reports | Select-Object -First 1
"reports in the data folder: $(Test-Path kdb-data\reports)   in the current folder: $(Test-Path reports)"

# A name that is not in the data folder is a folder in the current folder, as before.
kareladb sql market "SELECT count(*) AS brokers FROM brokers"

# A path always means that folder: .\reports is a new, empty database here.
kareladb sql .\reports "SHOW TABLES"
"reports in the current folder now: $(Test-Path reports)"
```

```text
table 'daily' created

1 row(s) inserted
day        | trades
-----------+-------
2026-09-10 |     32
(1 row, 0.4 ms)
database        kdb-data/reports
reports in the data folder: True   in the current folder: False
brokers
-------
      5
(1 row, 0.2 ms)
name | kind | partition | columns | rows
-----+------+-----------+---------+-----
(0 rows, 0.0 ms)
reports in the current folder now: True
```

## Output formats

### table (default)

For people. Numbers are right-aligned. At most 1000 rows are shown (change with `--max-rows`).

```powershell
kareladb sql market "SELECT symbol, ltp, pct_change FROM live_data LATEST ON timestamp PARTITION BY symbol"
```

```text
symbol | ltp   | pct_change
-------+-------+-----------
CITY   | 527.1 |       2.71
COAST  | 401.9 |        0.7
TELCO  | 897.7 |        1.9
VOLT   |   184 |      -0.86
(4 rows, 0.4 ms)
```

### csv

For Excel and scripts. The first line has the column names. There is no row limit.

```powershell
kareladb sql market "SELECT symbol, ltp, pct_change FROM live_data LATEST ON timestamp PARTITION BY symbol" --format csv
```

```text
symbol,ltp,pct_change
CITY,527.1,2.71
COAST,401.9,0.7
TELCO,897.7,1.9
VOLT,184,-0.86
```

- Text with a comma, quote or line break is put in `"double quotes"`.
- NULL is an empty field.
- Times are UTC, like `2026-09-10T05:15:00.000Z`.
- Messages like `3 row(s) inserted` are not printed in CSV.
- With many SELECT statements, the CSV blocks come one after another, each with its own header line. Use one SELECT per command when you save CSV.

To save a file: `kareladb sql market "SELECT ..." --format csv > prices.csv`. (In Windows PowerShell 5.1, `>` writes UTF-16. Use `| Set-Content prices.csv -Encoding UTF8` if another program must read the file.)

### json

For programs. One JSON array with one object per statement.

```powershell
kareladb sql market "SELECT symbol, ltp, pct_change FROM live_data LATEST ON timestamp PARTITION BY symbol" --format json
```

```text
[{"statement":"SELECT symbol, ltp, pct_change FROM live_data LATEST ON timestamp PARTITION BY symbol","columns":[{"name":"symbol","type":"SYMBOL"},{"name":"ltp","type":"DOUBLE"},{"name":"pct_change","type":"DOUBLE"}],"rows":[["CITY",527.1,2.71],["COAST",401.9,0.7],["TELCO",897.7,1.9],["VOLT",184,-0.86]],"rows_affected":0,"message":"","truncated":false}
]
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `statement` | The statement, as KarelaDB understood it |
| `columns` | Name and type of each column |
| `rows` | The rows. Each row is a list of values in column order. |
| `rows_affected` | Rows changed by INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE |
| `message` | For example `3 row(s) inserted` |
| `truncated` | `true` if there were more rows than `--max-rows` |

Values in JSON: numbers are numbers; TIMESTAMP and DATE are text (UTC); DECIMAL is text (to stay exact); NULL is `null`.

If a statement fails, the JSON of the statements before it is printed, and the error goes to the error output (stderr) with exit code 1.

### --max-rows

```powershell
kareladb sql market "SELECT time, symbol, close FROM ochl_minutes" --max-rows 3
```

```text
time                     | symbol | close
-------------------------+--------+------
2026-09-09T05:15:00.000Z | CITY   | 512.1
2026-09-09T05:16:00.000Z | CITY   | 511.9
2026-09-09T05:17:00.000Z | CITY   | 511.9
(3 rows, more not shown, 0.6 ms)
```

`--max-rows 0` means no limit. For a fixed number of rows in your result, `LIMIT` in the SQL is better: it also makes the query faster.

## PowerShell

### CSV to objects: ConvertFrom-Csv

```powershell
$rows = kareladb sql market "SELECT symbol, ltp, pct_change FROM live_data LATEST ON timestamp PARTITION BY symbol" --format csv | ConvertFrom-Csv

# Every value is text. Use [double] to compare numbers.
$rows | Where-Object { [double]$_.pct_change -gt 1 } | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

```text
symbol ltp   pct_change
------ ---   ----------
CITY   527.1 2.71      
TELCO  897.7 1.9
```

Without `[double]`, PowerShell compares text: `"10" -gt "9"` is false.

### JSON to objects: ConvertFrom-Json

In Windows PowerShell 5.1, join the lines with `Out-String` first:

```powershell
$json = kareladb sql market "SELECT symbol, sum(quantity) AS shares FROM trade_log WHERE date IN '2026-09-10' GROUP BY symbol ORDER BY shares DESC" --format json | Out-String
$result = ConvertFrom-Json $json

# One result per statement. rows is a list of rows; each row is a list of values.
foreach ($row in $result[0].rows) {
  "{0,-6} {1,6} shares" -f $row[0], $row[1]
}
```

```text
COAST    2850 shares
CITY      910 shares
TELCO     770 shares
VOLT      400 shares
```

JSON keeps numbers as numbers, so you do not need `[double]`.

### A loop: one CSV file per symbol

```powershell
foreach ($symbol in @("CITY", "COAST", "VOLT")) {
  $csv = kareladb sql market "SELECT symbol, time, close FROM ochl_day WHERE symbol = '$symbol' AND time IN '2026-09' ORDER BY time" --format csv
  $csv | Set-Content "close-$symbol.csv" -Encoding UTF8
  "$symbol : $(($csv | Measure-Object).Count - 1) rows saved to close-$symbol.csv"
}
```

```text
CITY : 8 rows saved to close-CITY.csv
COAST : 8 rows saved to close-COAST.csv
VOLT : 8 rows saved to close-VOLT.csv
```

Inside `"double quotes"`, PowerShell puts in the value of `$symbol`. The SQL text uses `'single quotes'`, so both work together.

**Never put text from users directly into SQL.** A symbol like `x' OR '1'='1` would change the query. Check such values first, for example with `if ($symbol -notmatch '^[A-Z0-9-]+$') { throw "bad symbol" }`.

### Exit codes in scripts

```powershell
kareladb sql market "INSERT INTO brokers VALUES (58, 'Northgate Securities')" 2>&1 | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
  Write-Output "The insert failed (exit code $LASTEXITCODE). Stop here."
}

kareladb check market | Out-Null
switch ($LASTEXITCODE) {
  0 { Write-Output "check: OK" }
  2 { Write-Output "check: DAMAGE FOUND - run kareladb repair" }
  default { Write-Output "check: could not run (exit code $LASTEXITCODE)" }
}
```

```text
The insert failed (exit code 1). Stop here.
check: OK
```

- `0` = OK, `1` = error, `2` = damage, `3` = the database needs a newer KarelaDB (chapter 2).
- `$LASTEXITCODE` changes after **every** program. Read it right after the `kareladb` command.
- `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` does **not** stop a script when `kareladb` fails. Check `$LASTEXITCODE` yourself.

### Non-English text (UTF-8)

Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends text into a pipe as ASCII by default. Letters outside English (Nepali, Chinese, accented letters, ...) then become `?`. Set UTF-8 first:

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends pipe text as ASCII unless you say UTF-8.
$OutputEncoding = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false

@"
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS names_np (symbol SYMBOL PRIMARY KEY, name_np STRING);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO names_np VALUES ('TELCO', 'नेपाल दूरसञ्चार');
"@ | Set-Content names.sql -Encoding UTF8

Get-Content names.sql -Raw -Encoding UTF8 | kareladb sql market -
kareladb sql market "SELECT symbol, name_np FROM names_np"
```

```text
table 'names_np' created

1 row(s) inserted
symbol | name_np        
-------+----------------
TELCO  | नेपाल दूरसञ्चार
(1 row, 0.2 ms)
```

- Save `.sql` files as **UTF-8**.
- Text in any language also works directly in the command line (`kareladb sql market "INSERT ... 'नेपाल'"`). If you see `????` after a pipe, see [chapter 12](12-troubleshooting.md#text-in-other-languages-looks-broken).
- PowerShell 7 already uses UTF-8.

## Daily backup script

This script makes a backup, deletes old backups, checks the database and writes a log. Run it every trading day **after 15:00 Nepal time**, when the market is closed.

It works when **no server is running** on the database (`kareladb backup` needs the database closed). If `kareladb serve` runs all the time, see [the server version](#if-kareladb-serve-runs-all-day) below.

Save as `daily-backup.ps1`:

```powershell
# daily-backup.ps1 - run after the market closes (15:00 Nepal time).
# Use full paths in a scheduled task, for example:
#   $Kdb = "D:\KarelaDB\build\bin\kareladb.exe"; $Data = "D:\kdb\market"; $Backups = "E:\kdb_backups"
$Kdb     = "kareladb"
$Data    = "market"
$Backups = "backups"
$Log     = "backup-log.txt"

Add-Content $Log "---- $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')"

# 2>&1 keeps error lines too; "$_" turns each line into plain text.
$out = & $Kdb backup $Data $Backups --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
Add-Content $Log $out
Add-Content $Log "backup exit code: $code"
if ($code -ne 0) { Write-Output "BACKUP FAILED, see $Log"; exit $code }

$out = & $Kdb check $Data 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
Add-Content $Log $out
Add-Content $Log "check exit code: $code"
if ($code -ne 0) { Write-Output "CHECK FOUND A PROBLEM, see $Log"; exit $code }

Write-Output "backup and check OK"
```

Run it:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\daily-backup.ps1
```

```text
backup and check OK
```

The log file:

```text
---- 2026-09-23 17:54:29
backup created and verified: backups/20260923-120929-906
  10 files, 190.8 KB, log up to 34
backup exit code: 0
checked 12 files (76.2 KB) and 1 log segments
OK: no damage found
check exit code: 0
```

Notes:

- **Put the backups on another disk** than the database (for example `E:\kdb_backups`). One broken disk must not destroy both.
- `--keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4` keeps the newest backup of each of the last 7 days and of the last 4 weeks. Older backups are deleted, and the script prints `removed old backup ...`.
- Backup folder names use **UTC** time: `20260923-120929-906` = 12:09:29 UTC = 17:54 Nepal time.

### If kareladb serve runs all day

A running server keeps the database open, so `kareladb backup` fails. Ask the server to make the backup instead. Start the server with `--backups E:\kdb_backups`, then:

```powershell
# daily-backup-server.ps1
$r = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:9900/api/backup"
"backup $($r.name): $($r.files) files, $($r.bytes) bytes"
$c = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:9900/api/check"
if (-not $c.ok) { Write-Output "CHECK FOUND A PROBLEM: $($c.problems -join '; ')"; exit 2 }
```

(If the server uses `--token`, add `-Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer <token>" }`.) The server keeps 7 daily and 4 weekly backups by itself. Chapter 8 shows the JSON of these two calls.

Simpler: no script at all. `kareladb serve ... --backups E:\kdb_backups --backup-schedule "daily 16:00" --backup-copy F:\kdb_copy` makes and checks the backups by itself, while the server keeps working ([chapter 21](21-protection.md#part-c-backups-on-a-schedule)).

### Windows Task Scheduler

Register the script to run Sunday to Thursday at 15:30. Run PowerShell **as Administrator**. Change the paths.

```powershell
$action  = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "powershell.exe" `
             -Argument "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File D:\kdb-work\daily-backup.ps1" `
             -WorkingDirectory "D:\kdb-work"
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Weekly -DaysOfWeek Sunday,Monday,Tuesday,Wednesday,Thursday -At 15:30
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "KarelaDB daily backup" -Action $action -Trigger $trigger `
  -Description "Backup and check the market KarelaDB database after market close"
```

(These Task Scheduler commands were **not run** while writing this tutorial, so they would not change the test PC. The script itself was run.)

- The time `15:30` is the **computer's** clock. Set the PC to Nepal time, or change the time.
- Test it once: `Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName "KarelaDB daily backup"`, then read the log file.
- In a task, use **full paths** in the script, because the task does not have your `PATH`.

## bash (Linux, macOS, Git Bash)

The same ideas in bash. Save as `report.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
DB=market

kareladb sql "$DB" "SELECT symbol, close FROM ochl_day WHERE time IN '2026-09-10'" --format csv > closes.csv
echo "saved $(( $(wc -l < closes.csv) - 1 )) rows"

kareladb sql "$DB" "SELECT nope FROM ochl_day" > /dev/null 2>&1
code=$?
if [ "$code" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "query failed with exit code $code"
fi

kareladb sql "$DB" - <<'SQL'
SELECT count(*) AS trades FROM trade_log;
SQL
```

```bash
bash ./report.sh
```

```text
saved 3 rows
query failed with exit code 1
trades
------
    32
(1 row, 0.3 ms)
```

- `<<'SQL' ... SQL` sends many lines of SQL into `kareladb sql ... -`. The quotes around `'SQL'` stop bash from changing `$` signs in the SQL.
- `kareladb sql "$DB" - < file.sql` sends a file.
- On Linux you can use `cron` for the daily backup: `30 15 * * 0-4 /home/kdb/daily-backup.sh` (Sunday=0 to Thursday=4, computer time).

(Tested with Git Bash on Windows.)

## Speed options for `kareladb serve`

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--memory <MB>` | 512 | Table data kept in memory. More is faster for big tables. Data stays on disk; only what queries need is loaded. |
| `--threads <N>` | half of the CPU threads | Threads for big queries and bulk writes. KarelaDB never uses more than half of the CPU threads. |
| `--cache-mb <MB>` | 64 | Memory for results of repeated queries. `0` turns the cache off. |
| `--sync-commits always\|batch` | always | `batch` is much faster for many small writes; a power cut can lose the last few confirmed writes, but never damages data. With `always`, writers that commit at the same moment still share one wait for the disk (group commit). |
| `--warm-indexes on\|off` | on | Build every index on a background thread right after a database opens, so the first query after a restart finds it ready. `off`: an index is built when a query first needs it. |
| `--reader-yield on\|off` | off | `on`: reads do not wait for a long trigger or `CALL`; they read the last committed rows. Also `KARELADB_READER_YIELD`. |

**The result cache.** When the same `SELECT` comes again (a dashboard that refreshes, a live page) and no table it reads has changed, KarelaDB answers from memory in a few microseconds.

- Any change to a table it read (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, line protocol, rollback) makes KarelaDB compute the result again.
- Changes of views, functions, procedures and tables clear the whole cache.
- Queries with `now()`, `random()`, `gen_random_uuid()`, password functions and similar are never kept.
- A `SELECT` inside your own open transaction is never taken from the cache.

```powershell
.\kareladb serve market --memory 2048 --cache-mb 128
```

## Protection options for `kareladb serve`

[Chapter 21](21-protection.md) explains them. They cost almost no speed.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--statement-timeout 30s` | 60s | Stop a statement that runs longer (`0` = no limit) |
| `--max-result-memory 512MB` | 1GB | Stop a query that keeps more rows in memory |
| `--max-groups N` | 5000000 | Stop a `GROUP BY` with more groups. (A `GROUP BY` that needs more than half of `--max-result-memory` does not stop: it puts groups in temporary files on disk and gives the same result, only slower.) |
| `--max-queries-per-user N` | 32 | Statements of one user at the same time |
| `--safe-updates` | off | Refuse `UPDATE`/`DELETE` without `WHERE` |
| `--read-only` | off | No changes at all (a report server) |
| `--trash-days N` | 7 | `DROP TABLE` keeps the table for `UNDROP TABLE` (also `kareladb sql` and `kareladb shell`) |
| `--audit on\|off`, `--audit-keep-days N` | on, forever | The audit log of logins, user changes, DDL and backups |
| `--backup-schedule "daily 16:00"` | off | Backups by themselves (needs `--backups`) |
| `--backup-copy <dir>` | none | A checked second copy of each scheduled backup |
| `--backup-warn-hours N` | 26 | Warn when the last good backup is older |
| `--drain-timeout 30s` | 30s | On stop (Ctrl+C or a service stop), running requests may finish this long; new ones get HTTP 503 |
| `--activity-log-size N` | 5000 | Recent events kept in memory for the console's Terminal (`0` = off) |

`kareladb sql` and `kareladb shell` have no timeouts or limits. `kareladb user reset-2fa <name>` turns two-factor login off while the server is stopped.

## Try it yourself

1. Save all CITY minute candles of 2026-09-10 to `city-minutes.csv`.
2. Write a PowerShell line that prints only the number of trade_log trades on 2026-09-10 (just the number).
3. Change the daily backup script so it also writes the size of the newest backup into the log (hint: `kareladb backups`).

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. ```powershell
   kareladb sql market "SELECT * FROM ochl_minutes WHERE symbol = 'CITY' AND time IN '2026-09-10' ORDER BY time" --format csv | Set-Content city-minutes.csv -Encoding UTF8
   ```
2. ```powershell
   (kareladb sql market "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM trade_log WHERE date IN '2026-09-10'" --format csv | ConvertFrom-Csv).n
   ```
   The answer is `24`.
3. After the backup lines, add:
   ```powershell
   $list = & $Kdb backups $Backups 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
   Add-Content $Log $list[1]    # line 2 = the newest backup
   ```

</details>
